teile.einleitung: The Titlis is a high mountain near Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden. It is 3,238 metres high and has a glacier on which there is snow all year round.
wichtigste: The Titlis is 3,238 metres high.
It lies near Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden, on the border with the canton of Bern.
On the Titlis there is a glacier with an ice cave.
Several cable cars lead up from Engelberg.
The last one is called the Rotair, and its cabin rotates.
At the top there is a suspension bridge over the abyss.

abschnitte.text: At **3,238 metres** the Titlis is one of the highest mountains in central Switzerland. Its summit is covered by a **glacier**. That is why there is snow up there even in summer. Like most glaciers in the Alps, the Titlis glacier is also getting smaller because of warmer temperatures.

From **Engelberg** you travel up the mountain in several stages. On the way you pass **Trübsee**. The last section leads on the **Titlis Rotair** to the top station on the Klein Titlis. Its cabin turns once completely round on itself during the ride. So every passenger sees the mountains all around.

In the **ice cave** you walk along a passage in the middle of the glacier ice. It is cold there even in summer. Outside, the **Titlis Cliff Walk** leads across a deep gorge. This **suspension bridge** is considered one of the highest in Europe. In the snow you can go sledging or glide over the glacier on a chairlift.

**Engelberg** is a holiday resort in a valley in the canton of Obwalden. Well known is the large **Engelberg Abbey**, which was founded as early as the Middle Ages. In winter many guests come to ski, in summer to walk. The Titlis attracts visitors from all over the world.

gewusst: The summit of the Titlis lies exactly on the border between Obwalden and Bern.
On the Titlis you can play in the snow even in midsummer.

teile.einleitung: The Waldenburg Railway is a railway in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. It runs from Liestal through the Waldenburg valley to Waldenburg and, until 2021, had the narrowest gauge in Switzerland at 75 centimetres.
wichtigste: The Waldenburg Railway runs from Liestal to Waldenburg.
It opened in 1880.
Until 2021 it had a gauge of only 75 centimetres.
That was the narrowest gauge in Switzerland.
After the conversion it runs on metre gauge.
Today BLT operates the railway.

abschnitte.text: The **Waldenburg Railway** opened in **1880**. It links **Liestal**, the main town of the canton of Basel-Landschaft, with **Waldenburg**. The route runs through the narrow **Waldenburg valley** and is about 13 kilometres long. In the past it ran with steam locomotives, later by electricity.

The **gauge** is the distance between the two rails. On the Waldenburg Railway it was only **75 centimetres**. That was the narrowest gauge of all public railways in Switzerland. Normal railways have 143.5 centimetres, many mountain railways one metre. The narrow track was cheap to build and fitted well in the narrow valley.

The old installations had grown old. So from **2021** the railway was completely renewed. In the process the gauge was widened to **one metre**. There are new tracks, new stops and modern trains. Today **BLT** (Baselland Transport) runs the railway as line 19.

gewusst: An old steam locomotive of the Waldenburg Railway is called “Gedeon Thommen”, after a watch manufacturer from Waldenburg.
The old Waldenburg Railway ran on its narrow track for over 140 years.

teile.einleitung: The Seelisberg Tunnel is a long motorway tunnel in central Switzerland. It links Nidwalden with the canton of Uri and is an important part of the north-south route through Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Seelisberg Tunnel is part of the A2 motorway.
It runs from Beckenried in Nidwalden to Seedorf in Uri.
It is around 9 kilometres long.
It opened in 1980.
The tunnel passes under the Seelisberg mountain, on the shore of Lake Lucerne.

abschnitte.text: The **Seelisberg Tunnel** is a tunnel on the **A2 motorway**, which runs from Basel to Chiasso. It begins at **Beckenried** in the canton of **Nidwalden** and ends at **Seedorf** in the canton of **Uri**. At around **9 kilometres** it is one of the longest road tunnels in Switzerland. It has **two tubes**, one for each direction of travel. So cars never drive in oncoming traffic.

The tunnel passes through the mountain near the village of **Seelisberg**. This lies on the southern shore of **Lake Lucerne**. In the past, cars heading south had to take the winding **Axenstrasse** or a boat. With the tunnel the journey became much faster and safer. Beyond Seedorf the road continues towards the Gotthard.

The Seelisberg Tunnel was built in the **1970s** and opened in **1980**. The **Gotthard road tunnel** opened in the same year. In the tunnel there are **emergency exits**, telephones and ventilation systems. Large fans make sure that exhaust fumes are blown out.

gewusst: Before the tunnel was built there was no motorway between Nidwalden and Uri.
Thousands of cars and lorries drive through the tunnel every day.

teile.einleitung: The University of St Gallen is a university in the city of St Gallen. It is often called HSG for short. It is especially well known for business and management.
wichtigste: The University of St Gallen is called HSG for short.
It was founded in 1898 as a commercial academy.
It is especially well known for economics and management.
You can also study law, international affairs and other subjects there.
Students come to St Gallen from many countries.

abschnitte.text: The institution was founded in **1898** as a **commercial academy**. At that time St Gallen was a rich city that traded **embroidery** and fabrics all over the world. Young people were to learn how to run trade and business. In time the small school became a **university**. The abbreviation HSG comes from its earlier German name, **Hochschule St. Gallen**.

The HSG is especially well known for **economics**. This includes subjects such as **business administration**, that is, how to run a company, and **national economics**, which deals with the economy of a whole country. Many of its programmes do well in international rankings. But you can also study **law**, international affairs and other subjects.

The university lies on the **Rosenberg** above the city of St Gallen. The buildings are modern and decorated with a lot of **art**. Works by well-known artists stand right in the corridors and lecture halls. There are also newer buildings, for example a learning centre for students.

At the HSG, young people from Switzerland and from **many other countries** study. Many courses are held in **English**. The university works closely with universities all over the world. Many students spend part of their studies abroad.

gewusst: Every year the St Gallen Symposium takes place at the HSG, a meeting of young people with experts from business and politics.
The abbey district of St Gallen with the famous Abbey Library is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

t147qpl2.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden shows an upright black bear on a white ground. Next to the bear are the letters V and R.
wichtigste: In the coat of arms of Appenzell Ausserrhoden stands a black bear.
The ground is white.
Next to the bear are the letters V and R.
V and R stand for “Usser Rhoden”.
The letters distinguish the coat of arms from that of Innerrhoden.

abschnitte.text: In the coat of arms of **Appenzell Ausserrhoden** a **black bear** stands upright on its hind legs. The ground is **white**. To the left and right of the bear are the letters **V** and **R**. They mean **“Usser Rhoden”** (in dialect), that is, the outer Rhoden.

A **Rhode** was formerly a district in the Appenzell region. In **1597** the land of Appenzell split into two parts. The reason was above all faith: the outer Rhoden became **Reformed** (Protestant), the inner ones stayed **Catholic**. This is how Ausserrhoden and Innerrhoden came about, which are now two cantons of their own.

Both Appenzells have the bear in their coat of arms. It comes from the time when the area belonged to the **Abbey of St Gallen**. So that the coats of arms can be told apart, Ausserrhoden added the letters **V** and **R**. The V is the old way of writing the letter U.

gewusst: In the past the letter U was often written like a V, so “VR” in the coat of arms stands for “Usser Rhoden”.
The bear in the Appenzell coat of arms goes back to the legend of Saint Gallus, who is said to have been helped by a bear.

teile.einleitung: The Vereina Tunnel is a railway tunnel of the Rhaetian Railway in the canton of Graubünden. It links Klosters in the Prättigau with the Lower Engadine and opened in 1999.
wichtigste: The Vereina Tunnel is in the canton of Graubünden.
It links Klosters with the Lower Engadine.
The tunnel is around 19 kilometres long.
It opened in 1999.
Cars are loaded onto the train and travel with it.
It belongs to the Rhaetian Railway.

abschnitte.text: The **Vereina Tunnel** is around **19 kilometres** long. It runs under the mountains from **Klosters** in the Prättigau to Sagliains near Susch and Lavin in the **Lower Engadine**. It opened in **1999**. The tunnel belongs to the **Rhaetian Railway**, which runs on narrow metre gauge in Graubünden.

If you want to go to the Engadine by car, you can load it onto the **car train**. You drive your car onto an open wagon and stay in it during the journey. After about 20 minutes you are on the other side. So you do not have to drive over a high pass. That is especially handy in winter.

Before it was built, the way into the Lower Engadine led over the **Flüela Pass**. This pass is over 2,300 metres high and is often closed in winter. Thanks to the tunnel, the Engadine can be reached easily all year round. Besides car trains, normal **passenger trains** also run through the tunnel. They link, for example, Landquart with Scuol.

During construction the workers had to drill and blast through hard rock. The tunnel is mostly **single-track**. In the middle there is a point where trains can pass each other. For the Rhaetian Railway the Vereina Tunnel was one of the biggest construction projects in its history.

gewusst: The Vereina Tunnel is one of the longest tunnels in the world for metre-gauge trains.
Both car trains and passenger trains of the Rhaetian Railway run through the Vereina Tunnel.

teile.einleitung: The St Gallen bratwurst is a famous speciality from eastern Switzerland. The pale sausage is made mainly from veal and is popular throughout Switzerland.
wichtigste: The St Gallen bratwurst is a white sausage made mainly from veal.
It comes from the canton of St Gallen and is known throughout Switzerland.
It is traditionally eaten with a Bürli.
Many people in St Gallen prefer to eat it without mustard.
The name is protected: only sausages made to the set recipe may be called this.

abschnitte.text: The **St Gallen bratwurst** is pale, almost white. It is made mainly from **veal**. Pork, bacon, **milk** and spices are added. The milk makes the sausage meat fine and pale. The sausage is first scalded and then fried on the grill or in a pan.

A **Bürli**, a small, crusty bread roll, goes with the St Gallen bratwurst. At stalls you often simply get the sausage in your hand with a Bürli. Many people in St Gallen think that a good bratwurst needs **no mustard**. The mustard would drown out the delicate flavour. Of course, if you like, you may still take mustard.

As early as the **Middle Ages** there were rules for butchers in St Gallen. They set out how sausages had to be made. Today the St Gallen bratwurst is a **protected geographical indication**. This means that only sausages from the region, made to the set recipe, may carry this name. In this way the quality stays the same.

Every autumn the **OLMA** takes place in St Gallen, a big trade fair for farming and food. There you can get the **OLMA bratwurst**, which is especially large. Many visitors come for the sausage too. The bratwurst is a real piece of **eastern Swiss culture**.

gewusst: A document from the year 1438 already contains rules from the St Gallen butchers for bratwursts.
The St Gallen bratwurst is also sold at many Swiss festivals and sporting events.

teile.einleitung: The Vogel Gryff is an old custom in Kleinbasel in the canton of Basel-Stadt. Every year in January three figures dance through the streets: the Vogel Gryff, the Leu and the Wilde Maa.
wichtigste: The Vogel Gryff takes place every year in January in Kleinbasel.
The three figures are called Vogel Gryff, Leu and Wilde Maa.
The Vogel Gryff is a griffin, the Leu a lion.
The Wilde Maa travels down the Rhine on a raft.
Three old honorary societies stand behind the custom.
During the dance the figures turn their backs on Grossbasel.

abschnitte.text: Three figures appear at the Vogel Gryff. The **Vogel Gryff** is a **griffin**, a mythical creature with the head of an eagle. The **Leu** is a lion. The **Wilde Maa** is a wild man with a small tree in his hand. Each figure belongs to one of the three **honorary societies** of Kleinbasel.

The day begins with the Wilde Maa's journey downstream. He stands on a **raft** and travels down the **Rhine**. Drummers and cannon shots accompany him. Then he steps ashore and meets the other two figures. Together they walk through the streets of Kleinbasel.

To the sound of drums the three figures dance in many places in **Kleinbasel**. A special moment is the dance on the **Mittlere Brücke** (Middle Bridge). There the figures turn their backs on Grossbasel on the other side of the Rhine. This is an old joke between the two parts of the city. Companions collect money for people in need.

The custom takes place every year on one day in **January**. The date alternates between the three honorary societies. For many people in Kleinbasel it is a festival day. Children like watching the figures, though some also feel a little respect for them.

gewusst: During the dance on the Middle Bridge the figures deliberately turn their backs on Grossbasel.
The Vogel Gryff is not a carnival custom but a festival day of its own for the people of Kleinbasel.

teile.einleitung: The Valais Blacknose sheep is an old breed of sheep from the Upper Valais. It has a white, curly fleece but a black face, black ears and black patches on its legs.
wichtigste: The Valais Blacknose sheep comes from the Valais.
Its fleece is white and curly.
Face, nose and ears are black.
Knees and feet also have black patches.
The sheep have spiral horns.
They are well adapted to life in the mountains.

abschnitte.text: The **Valais Blacknose sheep** is easy to recognise. Its **fleece** is thick, white and curly. The **face** with the nose and the **ears**, by contrast, are black. It also has black patches on its knees and feet. Both the rams and the females have spiral **horns**.

The breed comes from the **Upper Valais**, above all from the area around Visp. The sheep are strong and sure-footed. In summer they graze on high **alpine pastures** in the mountains. Their thick fleece protects them from cold and wind. That is why they are well adapted to the harsh climate.

In the past the sheep were kept mainly for **wool** and meat. Today they are also very popular for their funny looks. Many people call them the most beautiful sheep in the world. They are often seen in photos and on postcards. They are now also bred in other countries.

gewusst: Valais Blacknose sheep are often called “the cutest sheep in the world” and are even in demand abroad.

teile.einleitung: The Spalentor is an old town gate in Basel. It once belonged to the Basel town wall and is regarded as one of the most beautiful town gates in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Spalentor stands in the city of Basel in the canton of Basel-Stadt.
It was built around 1400 as part of the outer town wall.
It is one of three surviving town gates in Basel.
The gate has a colourful tiled roof and figures on its façade.
The road to Alsace led through the gate.

abschnitte.titel: A gate in the town wall
abschnitte.text: In the Middle Ages **Basel** was surrounded by a high **town wall**. Anyone who wanted to enter the town had to go through one of the **town gates**. The **Spalentor** was built around **1400**. It guarded the road that led west into **Alsace**. In the evening the gates were closed so that nobody could enter unseen.

The Spalentor consists of a tall, square **tower** and two round side towers. In the passage a heavy **portcullis** could be lowered. In front of it there used to be a ditch. The mighty wooden gates can still be seen today. In this way the people of Basel could defend their town against attackers.

The Spalentor is not only strong but also beautiful. Its roof is covered with **colour-glazed tiles** that form a pattern. On the outside stand **stone figures**, including a figure of **Mary** with the child. There are also coats of arms of the city of Basel. Today the gate is a **landmark** of Basel.

In the 19th century Basel grew rapidly. The town walls were no longer needed and were mostly pulled down. Only a few parts remained standing. Besides the Spalentor, the **St Alban Gate** and the **St Johann Gate** have also been preserved. Today trams run close past the Spalentor.

gewusst: The Spalentor is one of the cultural properties of national significance.
From the Spalentor the Spalenvorstadt, with many old houses, leads into the old town.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss National Park in the Engadine is the only national park in Switzerland. Here nature has been allowed to develop freely for over a hundred years, without people interfering.
wichtigste: The Swiss National Park lies in the canton of Graubünden, in the Engadine and the Val Müstair.
It was founded in 1914 and is the oldest national park in the Alps.
It covers around 170 square kilometres.
In the park nature is strictly protected: you must not leave the paths.
There you can watch deer, chamois, ibex and marmots.
The visitor centre is in Zernez.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss National Park** was founded on **1 August 1914**. It was the first national park in the Alps. The idea was to leave a piece of land entirely to nature. Since then there has been no hunting, no fishing, no logging and no grazing of livestock. Fallen trees stay where they are and become food for fungi and beetles.

Many large wild animals live in the park. Especially well known are the **red deer**, which you can hear roaring in autumn. There are also **chamois**, **ibex** and many **marmots**. **Golden eagles** circle in the sky, along with the **bearded vulture**, which has been reintroduced in the Alps. With binoculars you can often spot the animals from far away.

So that the animals are left in peace, **strict rules** apply in the park. You may only walk on the marked paths. Dogs are forbidden, as are bikes away from the roads. You must not pick flowers, take stones away or light fires. Staying overnight is only allowed in the huts provided.

The national park is also a large **open-air laboratory**. For decades researchers have been observing how forest, meadows and wildlife change without human influence. In **Zernez** stands the **visitor centre** with an exhibition. The road over the **Ofen Pass** runs through the park. Many hiking trails invite you to go on outings.

gewusst: The Swiss National Park is strictly protected, far more strictly than most other parks in Switzerland.
In the Val Trupchun you can often watch whole herds of deer in autumn.

teile.einleitung: Schwyz is the main town of the canton of the same name in central Switzerland. The canton is one of the founding places of the Swiss Confederation and gave its name to the whole country.
wichtigste: The main town of the canton of Schwyz is also called Schwyz.
The town lies at the foot of the two Mythen peaks.
Together with Uri and Unterwalden, Schwyz is one of the three original cantons.
The names “Switzerland” and “Swiss” come from the name Schwyz.
In the Federal Charters Museum in Schwyz lies the Federal Charter of 1291.

abschnitte.titel: A main town by the mountain
abschnitte.text: The main town of the canton of Schwyz has the same name as the canton: **Schwyz**. It lies in a basin between Lake Lauerz and Lake Lucerne. Behind the town rise the two rocky peaks **Grosser Mythen** and **Kleiner Mythen**. In the town centre stand the parish church, the **town hall** and many old mansions. The cantonal government and the cantonal council meet here.

With **Uri** and **Unterwalden**, Schwyz is one of the three **original cantons**. In 1291 they made an alliance, which is called the **Federal Charter**. This valuable document is kept in the **Federal Charters Museum** in Schwyz. There you can look at it together with old flags. The Confederation later grew to include many other places.

Because the people of Schwyz played an important role early on, all the Confederates soon came to be called “**Schwyzers**”. From this came the name **Switzerland** (“Schweiz”). The canton's flag is red with a small white cross in the upper corner. The **Swiss cross** on the national flag goes back to this emblem.

The canton of Schwyz includes well-known places such as **Einsiedeln** with its abbey, **Küssnacht** and **Lachen** on Lake Zurich. In the district of **Ibach** in the municipality of Schwyz, the famous **Swiss army knives** by Victorinox are made. The canton has mountains, lakes and a lot of farming. In winter many people go skiing in the areas around the Mythen.

gewusst: The Grosser Mythen is 1,898 metres high and can be climbed on a steep hiking trail.
In dialect, people also say “Schwyz” for the whole of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Ornithological Institute in Sempach in the canton of Lucerne looks after the birds of Switzerland. It researches how they are doing and works to protect them.
wichtigste: The Swiss Ornithological Institute has its headquarters in Sempach on Lake Sempach.
It was founded in 1924 and is a non-profit foundation.
It researches native birds and bird migration.
It works to protect endangered bird species and their habitats.
A visitor centre shows young and old the world of birds.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Ornithological Institute** counts and observes the birds across the whole of Switzerland. Many volunteers report which species they have seen and where. In this way we know which birds are becoming more common and which are becoming rarer. The results appear, for example, in a **breeding bird atlas**, a large map of birdlife. The institute also researches **bird migration** in autumn and spring.

An important method is **ringing**. A bird is given a light ring with a number on its leg. If it is found later in another place, we know where it flew. This is how it was discovered that many migratory birds from Switzerland spend the winter in Africa. Today tiny devices that record the route are also used.

Many birds need hedges, old trees, wetlands or flower meadows. The institute advises municipalities, farmers and authorities on how to preserve such **habitats**. It also helps with projects for endangered species. In its **care station**, injured birds are looked after and, where possible, released again.

In Sempach there is a modern **visitor centre** run by the institute. There you can learn a lot about birds in an exhibition, listen to their songs and watch them outside in the garden. The centre lies on the shore of **Lake Sempach**. Many school classes visit it.

gewusst: Around 200 different bird species breed in Switzerland.
Some migratory birds from Switzerland fly thousands of kilometres to Africa and back every year.

teile.einleitung: The Black Madonna of Einsiedeln is a famous figure of Mary in the canton of Schwyz. It stands in the Chapel of Grace in the monastery church of Einsiedeln. People have made pilgrimages to it for centuries.
wichtigste: The Black Madonna stands in the monastery church of Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz.
It shows Mary with the infant Jesus.
Its face and hands are dark.
It stands in the Chapel of Grace inside the church.
Einsiedeln is the best-known place of pilgrimage in Switzerland.
The monastery belongs to the Benedictine order.

abschnitte.text: The **Black Madonna** is a carved wooden figure. It shows **Mary** holding the infant Jesus in her arm. The present figure dates from the 15th century. It usually wears a magnificent robe, which is changed according to the church festival. The face and hands are coloured dark.

It is thought that the figure became dark over the years from the **smoke** of many candles and oil lamps. When it was restored later, it was deliberately left dark. People knew and revered it that way. That is why it is still called the Black Madonna.

**Einsiedeln Abbey** was founded in the 10th century. Before that the hermit **Meinrad** is said to have lived here, which is where the name of the place comes from (“Einsiedler” means hermit). The present large **Baroque church** was built in the 18th century. The **Chapel of Grace** with the Madonna stands in the middle of the church.

A **pilgrimage** is a journey to a holy place, often on foot. Every year a great many pilgrims come to Einsiedeln. They pray before the Madonna or light a candle. Einsiedeln also lies on the **Way of St James**, which leads all the way to Santiago de Compostela in Spain.

gewusst: In front of the abbey there is a large square with a fountain of Mary, from which many pilgrims drink.
There are also famous Black Madonnas in other places in Europe, such as Altötting in Bavaria.

teile.einleitung: The Stadtlounge (City Lounge) is a special square in the city of St Gallen. It is covered in a red surface and looks like a giant living room in the open air.
wichtigste: The Stadtlounge lies in the Bleicheli district of the city of St Gallen.
The ground, benches and even a table are covered in red plastic.
The artist Pipilotti Rist designed it together with the architect Carlos Martinez.
The Stadtlounge opened in 2005.
The square is meant to feel like a living room for everyone.

abschnitte.text: The **Stadtlounge** is a square in the **Bleicheli district** of St Gallen. The ground is covered with a soft **red surface** made of plastic. The red carpet also stretches over benches and over a large **table**. So the square looks like a **living room** under the open sky. That is why many people also call it the “red square”.

The Stadtlounge was designed by the artist **Pipilotti Rist** and the architect **Carlos Martinez**. Pipilotti Rist grew up in the Rhine Valley in the canton of St Gallen and is internationally known, above all for her video art. Above the square hang large, round **lights** that look like floating lamps. They bathe the square in soft light in the evening. The Stadtlounge opened in **2005**.

The Stadtlounge is meant to be a place to **linger**. You can sit down, take a break or meet friends. Around the square stand office buildings, shops and restaurants. For tourists the Stadtlounge is a popular photo spot. It shows how art can change a part of a city.

gewusst: For the Stadtlounge a whole street space was designed like an indoor room.
The soft surface feels quite different from ordinary asphalt.

teile.einleitung: The Simplon Tunnel is a railway tunnel under the Simplon. Since 1906 it has linked the Valais with Italy, and when it opened it was the longest tunnel in the world.
wichtigste: The Simplon Tunnel links Brig in the Valais with Iselle in Italy.
It opened in 1906.
It is almost 20 kilometres long.
When it opened it was the longest tunnel in the world.
It consists of two tubes; the second was finished in 1921.

abschnitte.text: The **Simplon Tunnel** runs under the mountains by the **Simplon Pass**. It begins in **Brig** in the canton of the **Valais** and ends in **Iselle** in **Italy**. The tunnel is just under **20 kilometres** long. It is part of an important railway line that links northern Europe with Milan by way of Switzerland. Trains take about a quarter of an hour to pass through.

Construction began in **1898** from both sides at the same time. The workers struggled with great **heat** in the mountain and with water breaking in. To cool the tunnel, cold water was channelled in. Many workers came from Italy. People also lost their lives in the heavy work.

When it opened in **1906**, the Simplon Tunnel was the **longest tunnel in the world**. It held this record for several decades. Next to the first tube a second was built, which was finished in **1921**. In this way a track in each tube can carry trains in one direction. The border between Switzerland and Italy runs right through the middle of the tunnel.

A road also runs over the **Simplon Pass**, built as long ago as the time of **Napoleon**. In winter the journey there can be difficult. So **car trains** also run through the Simplon Tunnel between Brig and Iselle. You drive your car onto a railway wagon and are pulled through the mountain.

gewusst: Inside the Simplon Tunnel it became so hot during construction that work was only possible with cooling.
The famous Simplon-Orient-Express also used to run through the Simplon Tunnel.

teile.einleitung: The Stoosbahn is a funicular in the canton of Schwyz. It runs from Schwyz up to the car-free mountain village of Stoos and is considered the steepest funicular in the world.
wichtigste: The Stoosbahn opened in December 2017.
It links the valley station Schlattli near Schwyz with the village of Stoos.
Its steepest gradient is 110 per cent.
The cabins are round like barrels and rotate during the journey.
This way passengers always stand upright, however steep the track is.
It replaced an older funicular from 1933.

abschnitte.text: A **funicular** runs on rails along the ground. A strong **steel cable** pulls the cars up the mountain. Often two cars are attached to the same cable: when one goes up, the other comes down. In this way they balance each other and save energy.

A gradient of **100 per cent** means that for every metre of track you rise one metre. That corresponds to an angle of 45 degrees. At its steepest point the Stoosbahn is even steeper, namely **110 per cent**. That is why it is considered the **steepest funicular in the world**. Along the route it also passes through tunnels and over bridges.

The cars consist of several round cabins that look like **drums**. Because the gradient changes along the way, the cabins rotate slowly. This keeps the floor level at all times. So passengers do not have to hold on to a sloping wall.

**Stoos** lies on a sunny terrace high above the basin of Schwyz. The village is **car-free** and can only be reached by cable railways. In winter many people come to ski, in summer to walk. Well known is the ridge walk from the Klingenstock to the Fronalpstock with a view of Lake Lucerne.

gewusst: The building work took many years because the route is so steep and hard to reach.
There are no cars on Stoos, so it is especially quiet there.

teile.einleitung: Lake Uri is the southernmost arm of Lake Lucerne and lies in the canton of Uri. It is surrounded by steep rock walls and is one of the places closely linked with the founding story of Switzerland.
wichtigste: Lake Uri is the southernmost part of Lake Lucerne.
It stretches from Brunnen to Flüelen.
At Flüelen the Reuss flows into the lake.
On the western shore lies the Rütli meadow.
On the eastern shore the Axenstrasse runs along the cliffs.
The hiking trail “Swiss Path” runs around the lake.

abschnitte.text: Lake Uri is the southernmost arm of **Lake Lucerne**. It lies between Brunnen in the canton of Schwyz and **Flüelen** in the canton of Uri. On both sides steep rock walls and high mountains rise straight out of the water. At Flüelen the **Reuss** flows into the lake. That is why Lake Uri looks almost like a fjord.

On the western shore lies the **Rütli meadow**. According to tradition, representatives of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden met there for the Rütli Oath. On the eastern shore stands **Tell's Chapel** at the Tellsplatte. It recalls the legend of William Tell, who is said to have leapt here from the boat of his enemies. Both places are easy to reach by boat.

On the eastern shore the **Axenstrasse** runs from Brunnen to Flüelen. It is partly cut into the rock and runs through tunnels and galleries. The hiking trail **“Swiss Path”** runs around Lake Uri. It was opened in 1991 for the 700th anniversary of the Confederation. Each canton has a stretch of path of its own.

The **foehn**, a warm, strong downslope wind from the south, often blows across Lake Uri. Then the lake can become very choppy. For sailors and windsurfers that is exciting, but for small boats it is dangerous. In strong foehn, storm lights on the shore warn people on the water.

gewusst: The Rütli meadow was bought in 1859 with donations from all over Switzerland and then given to the Confederation.
On the Swiss Path the stretches are as long as the canton has inhabitants: the more inhabitants, the longer the stretch.

teile.einleitung: The Titlis Rotair is an aerial cable car near Engelberg in the canton of Obwalden. What makes it special: the cabin turns completely around once during the ride.
wichtigste: The Rotair runs from Stand to the top station on the Klein Titlis.
During the ride the cabin turns once through 360 degrees.
It opened in 1992.
It was the first rotating aerial cable car in the world.
On the way it glides over the Titlis glacier.

abschnitte.text: In the Rotair you stand on a **rotating floor**. During the ride it turns slowly all the way round, that is, through **360 degrees**. So nobody has to fight for the best place at the window. Every passenger sees in turn the rock walls, the glacier and the valley of Engelberg.

The Rotair is the last stage on the way from **Engelberg** to the Titlis. It starts at the **Stand** station and runs up to the top station on the **Klein Titlis**, at over 3,000 metres. On the way it glides over the **glacier** and over deep crevasses in the ice. The ride lasts only a few minutes.

When the Rotair opened in **1992**, it was the **first rotating aerial cable car in the world**. Later, similar rotating cable cars were also built in other places. The Rotair attracts many guests from all over the world.

gewusst: The name Rotair is made up of “rotation” and “air”.
Many people have room in the cabin at the same time.

teile.einleitung: The Sitter is a river in eastern Switzerland. It rises in the Alpstein, flows through the village of Appenzell and past St Gallen, and finally joins the Thur.
wichtigste: The Sitter rises in the Alpstein.
It flows through the village of Appenzell.
Then it flows past the town of St Gallen to the west.
At Bischofszell it joins the Thur.
Many high bridges cross the Sitter.

abschnitte.text: The **Sitter** begins in the **Alpstein**, the mountain range around the **Säntis**. Several mountain streams come together there, including water from the area of the **Seealpsee**. At **Weissbad** the streams unite to form the Sitter. Then the river flows through the village of **Appenzell**, the main town of Appenzell Innerrhoden.

After Appenzell the Sitter has cut deep into the terrain. This has created narrow, steep valleys called **Tobel** (ravines). To cross them, many high **bridges** were built. Well known are the bridges over the **Sittertobel** near St Gallen, which carry roads and railway lines. On a bridge trail you can visit many of them on foot.

West of the town of **St Gallen** the Sitter flows on to the north. The **Urnäsch**, a river from the Appenzell Hinterland, also flows into it. At **Bischofszell** in the canton of Thurgau the Sitter flows into the **Thur**. The Thur in turn flows into the **Rhine**. In this way the water from the Alpstein finally reaches the North Sea.

gewusst: Around St Gallen there are so many bridges that a hiking trail of its own leads to them.
On hot summer days many people swim in the Sitter.

teile.einleitung: Toblerone is a triangular chocolate that was invented in Bern in 1908. It is known all over the world, and many people think of mountain peaks when they see its shape.
wichtigste: Toblerone was invented in Bern in 1908.
Its inventors were Theodor Tobler and Emil Baumann.
The chocolate contains honey and almond nougat.
The name combines “Tobler” with “torrone”, an Italian nougat.
The shape is made up of many small triangles.
A bear is hidden in the logo, the heraldic animal of Bern.

abschnitte.text: **Theodor Tobler** ran a chocolate factory in Bern. Together with his cousin **Emil Baumann** he developed a new chocolate in **1908**. It contained **honey** and **almond nougat**. The new kind was given the name **Toblerone**, from “Tobler” and the Italian word **“torrone”** for nougat.

Toblerone is shaped in a row of **triangles** and comes in a triangular pack. Many people think of the **Swiss mountains** when they see it. For a long time the **Matterhorn** was shown on the pack. How exactly the shape came about is told in different ways.

A **bear** is hidden in the Toblerone logo. You can see it if you look closely at the mountain shape in the picture. The bear is the **heraldic animal** of the city of Bern. In this way the pack recalls the place where the chocolate was invented.

Today Toblerone is sold in over a hundred countries, especially often at **airports**. For many years the brand has belonged to large international food companies. In recent years part of the production has been moved abroad. Because the chocolate therefore no longer comes entirely from Switzerland, the Matterhorn disappeared from the pack from 2023.

gewusst: Toblerone is still made in Bern today.
Toblerone comes in many sizes, from very small to very large bars.

teile.einleitung: The Thur is a river in eastern Switzerland. It rises in the Toggenburg, flows through the cantons of St Gallen, Thurgau and Zurich and joins the Rhine. The canton of Thurgau is named after it.
wichtigste: The Thur rises in the uppermost Toggenburg in the canton of St Gallen.
It flows through St Gallen, Thurgau and Zurich.
It flows into the Rhine.
The canton of Thurgau takes its name from the Thur.
The Thur does not flow through a large lake, so its water level can rise quickly.

abschnitte.text: The Thur begins in the mountains near the **Säntis** in the upper **Toggenburg**. It flows north through the whole valley. Then it turns west and crosses the **canton of Thurgau**. It flows past places such as **Bischofszell** and **Weinfelden**. In the Zurich Weinland it finally joins the **Rhine**.

The name **Thurgau** means roughly “area on the Thur”. A **Gau** was formerly a word for a landscape or region. The river flows right across the canton. That is why it is still important for Thurgau today. The main town of the canton is **Frauenfeld**.

Many large Swiss rivers flow through a **lake**. The lake takes in a lot of water during heavy rain. The Thur has no such lake. So after thunderstorms or during the snowmelt its water often rises very **quickly**. In the past there were therefore repeated **floods**. Today embankments and wider river beds protect the villages.

In many places the Thur was once forced into a straight bed. Today in some places it is given **more room** again. This is called **renaturation**. It creates gravel banks, floodplains and habitats for fish, birds and plants. You can also walk and cycle well along the bank.

gewusst: In the Toggenburg, near Unterwasser, there are the Thur waterfalls.
At Bischofszell the Sitter flows into the Thur.

teile.einleitung: The Council of States is one of the two chambers of the Swiss Parliament. The cantons are represented in it. Together with the National Council it forms the Federal Assembly.
wichtigste: The Council of States has 46 members.
20 cantons elect two members each.
Six cantons with half a cantonal vote elect one member each, for example Nidwalden.
The Council of States represents the cantons, the National Council the people.
Both chambers have equal say.
The members are elected every four years.

abschnitte.text: The Swiss Parliament is called the **Federal Assembly**. It consists of the **National Council** with 200 members and the **Council of States** with 46 members. In the National Council larger cantons get more seats. In the Council of States, however, every canton counts for roughly the same. In this way small cantons also have a strong voice. This arrangement has existed since the Federal Constitution of 1848.

Most cantons send **two members** to the Council of States. Obwalden, Nidwalden, Basel-Stadt, Basel-Landschaft, Appenzell Ausserrhoden and Appenzell Innerrhoden have **one seat** each. They used to be called **half-cantons**; today people speak of cantons with half a cantonal vote. So Zurich, with a great many inhabitants, has the same number of seats as the small canton of Uri.

How the members of the Council of States are elected is decided by each canton itself. In most cantons the person who gets the most votes wins. This is called the **majority system**. Some cantons, such as Jura and Neuchâtel, elect by a different procedure. Elections are held every four years, usually together with the National Council.

abschnitte.titel: What the Council of States does
abschnitte.text: The Council of States debates **laws** and the federal budget. A new law only takes effect if **both chambers** agree. If they disagree, the matter goes back and forth between them. Together the National Council and Council of States also elect the members of the **Federal Council**. The Council of States meets in the Federal Palace in Bern.

gewusst: The Council of States is often called the “small chamber” and the National Council the “large chamber”.
When the Parliament was set up in 1848, the US Senate served as a model.

teile.einleitung: Sion, called Sitten in German, is the main town of the canton of the Valais. The old town in the Rhône valley is known for its two castle hills and its long history.
wichtigste: Sion (German: Sitten) is the main town of the Valais.
The town lies in the Rhône valley.
Above the old town stand the two hills of Valère and Tourbillon.
On Valère stands a church with one of the oldest playable organs in the world.
In Sion people mainly speak French.
Sion has been the seat of a bishop for many centuries.

abschnitte.text: **Sion** is the main town of the canton of the **Valais**. In German the town is called **Sitten**. It lies in the middle of the broad valley of the **Rhône**. The Valais government and the cantonal parliament, the **Grand Council**, work here. Most people in Sion speak **French**, because the town lies in the French-speaking part of the canton.

Two rocky hills rise above the old town. On one stands the **Basilica of Valère**, a fortified church from the Middle Ages. On the other lie the ruins of **Tourbillon Castle**. The two hills are the landmark of Sion. From the top you have a wide view over the Rhône valley and the vineyards.

In the Basilica of Valère there is a special **organ**. It dates from the Middle Ages and is regarded as one of the **oldest playable organs in the world**. Concerts take place there every summer. Part of the **Valais History Museum** is also housed in the building.

Sion is one of the oldest towns in Switzerland. People were already living here in Roman times. Since the early Middle Ages Sion has been the seat of the **bishop** of the Valais. Around the town, many **vines** grow on sunny slopes. The Valais is the biggest wine-growing canton in Switzerland.

gewusst: The Valais is one of the sunniest regions of Switzerland, which is why apricots also thrive there.
The football club FC Sion has won the Swiss Cup very many times.

teile.einleitung: Tell's Chapel stands right on the shore of Lake Uri near Sisikon in the canton of Uri. It recalls the legend of William Tell, who is said to have saved himself here by leaping out of a boat.
wichtigste: Tell's Chapel stands at the Tellsplatte near Sisikon.
Lake Uri is the southernmost part of Lake Lucerne.
According to the legend, Tell leapt here from the boat of the bailiff Gessler.
The present chapel was built in the 19th century.
Inside, large murals show scenes from the Tell legend.

abschnitte.text: According to the legend, **William Tell** was taken prisoner after shooting the apple from his son's head. The bailiff **Gessler** wanted to take him across the lake by boat. A violent **storm** blew up, and Tell was put at the helm. He steered the boat close to the shore and leapt onto a **ledge of rock**. This spot is now called the **Tellsplatte**.

A small chapel already stood at the Tellsplatte centuries ago. The present **Tell's Chapel** was built in the 19th century. Inside, the artist **Ernst Stückelberg** painted large **murals**. They show the shot at the apple, Tell's leap and further scenes from the legend. The chapel stands so close to the water that you can also see it clearly from a boat.

Many visitors come by **boat** across Lake Uri. Others walk the **Swiss Path**, a hiking trail around Lake Uri. From the Axenstrasse a footpath leads down to the chapel. Opposite, on the other shore of the lake, lies the **Rütli meadow**.

Whether William Tell really lived has not been proved. Most experts regard him as a **legendary figure**. Even so, he is an important figure for Switzerland. He stands for courage and for the desire for **freedom**. Tell's Chapel is therefore a well-known place of remembrance.

gewusst: The Tellsplatte is a popular stop for boats on Lake Uri.
The story of Tell's leap became famous worldwide through Friedrich Schiller's play “William Tell”.

teile.einleitung: Lake Walen lies in eastern Switzerland between the canton of St Gallen and the canton of Glarus. It is surrounded by steep mountains, above all by the Churfirsten on the northern shore.
wichtigste: Lake Walen lies between the cantons of St Gallen and Glarus.
The northern shore belongs to the canton of St Gallen.
Part of the southern shore belongs to the canton of Glarus.
On the northern shore the Churfirsten rise steeply.
The village of Quinten can only be reached by boat or on foot.
The lake lies between Weesen and Walenstadt.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Walen** lies between **Weesen** in the west and **Walenstadt** in the east. It is about 15 kilometres long and quite narrow. On the northern shore the **Churfirsten** rise almost vertically like a rock wall. On the southern shore too the mountains are high and steep. The water often shimmers green or turquoise.

The lake belongs to two cantons. The **northern shore** belongs entirely to the canton of **St Gallen**. On the **southern shore** one part lies in the canton of **Glarus**, for example near Mühlehorn; the rest belongs to St Gallen. So the canton of Glarus shares Lake Walen with St Gallen.

On the northern shore lies the little village of **Quinten**. It has no road and can only be reached by **boat** or on foot. Because it lies sheltered from the Churfirsten and sunny, the climate there is mild. That is why even **vines** and figs grow in Quinten. Nearby the **Seerenbach Falls** tumble over the rocks.

Because the northern shore is so steep, the railway and motorway run along the **southern shore**. The A3 motorway runs there through many tunnels and galleries. The railway line from Zurich to Chur also runs along the lake. From the train you have a lovely view of the Churfirsten.

gewusst: The Seerenbach Falls near Betlis are among the highest waterfalls in Switzerland.
Because of its mild climate Quinten is sometimes called the “Riviera of eastern Switzerland”.

teile.einleitung: Trogen is a small village in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden. Although it has only a few inhabitants, the cantonal courts sit here. Trogen is also known for its beautiful houses and the Pestalozzi Children's Village.
wichtigste: Trogen lies in the canton of Appenzell Ausserrhoden.
The cantonal courts have their seat in Trogen.
The government and parliament meet in Herisau.
Until 1997 the Landsgemeinde was held alternately in Trogen and Hundwil.
In Trogen stands the Pestalozzi Children's Village, founded in 1946.

abschnitte.text: Appenzell Ausserrhoden does not have a single main town for everything. The **government** and **parliament** are in **Herisau**. The canton's **courts** sit in **Trogen**. So two municipalities share the tasks that elsewhere are held by a single main town. This has to do with the history of the canton.

In the past, those entitled to vote in Ausserrhoden decided matters at the **Landsgemeinde**. This is an assembly in the open air, at which people vote by raising a hand. It was held alternately in **Trogen** and in **Hundwil**. In **1997** those entitled to vote decided to abolish the Landsgemeinde. Today voting is done at the ballot box.

On the **Landsgemeindeplatz** in Trogen stand large, magnificent houses. Many of them were built by the **Zellweger** family. They became rich in the 18th century through the **linen trade** and fabrics. The houses show how prosperous the place was at that time. Trogen also has a **cantonal school**.

After the **Second World War** the **Pestalozzi Children's Village** was founded in Trogen in **1946**. Here children from countries affected by war found a home. It is named after the educator **Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi**. Today the foundation works for education and peaceful coexistence.

gewusst: The Trogenerbahn takes you directly from St Gallen to Trogen.
The Pestalozzi Children's Village lies on a hill above the village.

teile.einleitung: The voting age sets the age from which you may vote and take part in elections. In Switzerland it is mostly 18 years, but in the canton of Glarus even 16-year-olds can have a say.
wichtigste: The voting age is the age from which you may vote and elect.
For federal votes in Switzerland it is 18 years.
In 2007 Glarus became the first canton to introduce a voting age of 16.
This was decided by the Landsgemeinde in Glarus.
In Glarus young people from 16 can have a say on cantonal and municipal questions.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland citizens can often **vote** on issues and **elect** their representatives. The **voting age** sets the age from which you may do this. For **federal** votes and elections it is **18 years**. Until **1991** it was still 20 years. Then the people and the cantons agreed to lower it to 18.

In the canton of **Glarus** a special voting age applies. At the **Landsgemeinde** (open-air assembly) in **2007**, those entitled to vote decided to lower the age to **16 years**. Glarus was thus the **first canton** in Switzerland with a voting age of 16. So young people can have a say on cantonal and municipal questions from the age of 16. For federal votes, the age of 18 applies to them too.

The **Landsgemeinde** is an old form of direct democracy. Once a year those entitled to vote gather in the open air on the Zaunplatz in **Glarus**. They vote by holding up their **voting card**. Today the Landsgemeinde exists only in Glarus and in **Appenzell Innerrhoden**. So in Glarus even 16-year-olds can raise their hand in the middle of the square.

Whether people should vote as early as 16 is debated again and again in Switzerland. **Supporters** say that young people are affected by many decisions and should have a say early. **Opponents** say that the rights and duties of adulthood should go together, that is, from 18. Several cantons have voted on it, and the results have differed.

gewusst: Women in Switzerland have only been able to vote and stand in elections at federal level since 1971.
Even in Glarus you can only be elected to an office from the age of 18.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Science Center Technorama in Winterthur is a hands-on museum. Instead of just looking at things, you can experiment and marvel for yourself.
wichtigste: The Technorama stands in Winterthur in the canton of Zurich.
It opened in 1982.
There are hundreds of experiments to try out.
The themes range from light and magnetism to water and perception.
It is one of the largest science centres in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: At the Technorama the rule is: **please touch!** At many stations you press, turn or pull things yourself. In this way you discover how **physics**, **chemistry** and **nature** work. Short texts explain what is happening. You learn by trying things out yourself, not by listening.

There are areas on **light and colours**, on **magnetism** and **electricity** and on **water**. You can, for example, create whirlpools in water or see shadows in bright colours. Other stations show how easily our eyes can be fooled. Such **optical illusions** are very popular with children and adults.

Besides the experiments there are **demonstrations**. Experts show experiments that you could not do on your own. Well known are the demonstrations with **high voltage**, in which big sparks crackle. School classes also often visit the Technorama to learn more about the natural sciences.

**Winterthur** is the second-largest city in the canton of Zurich. The city was long an important place for industry and mechanical engineering. Today it is also known for its many **museums**. The Technorama is among the most visited of them.

gewusst: At the Technorama there are also experiments outdoors in the park.
Many stations work entirely without electricity, using only water, light or gravity.

teile.einleitung: Stein am Rhein is a small town in the canton of Schaffhausen. It is famous for its old town with brightly painted house façades and is one of the most beautiful places in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Stein am Rhein lies in the canton of Schaffhausen on the Rhine.
Here the Rhine flows out of the Untersee, part of Lake Constance.
In the old town many houses are painted with colourful pictures.
Hohenklingen Castle stands above the little town.
In 1972 Stein am Rhein was the first place to receive the Wakker Prize.

abschnitte.titel: A little town on the Rhine
abschnitte.text: **Stein am Rhein** lies in the canton of **Schaffhausen**. At this spot the **Rhine** flows out of the **Untersee**, the western part of Lake Constance. The little town is small but very old. Its medieval **old town** is well preserved. Many visitors arrive by boat from Schaffhausen or from Lake Constance.

Best known is the **Rathausplatz** (town hall square). All around stand old **half-timbered houses** and town houses. Many of them are decorated with large, colourful **façade paintings**. The pictures show stories from the Bible, from history and from legends. Many houses also have beautiful **oriel windows** and names of their own, for example “Zum weissen Adler” (“At the White Eagle”).

On the bank of the Rhine stands the former **St Georgen Monastery**. Today it is a museum and shows how the monks lived in the past. High above the little town towers **Hohenklingen Castle**. From there you have a lovely view of Stein am Rhein, the Rhine and the Untersee. You can walk up on foot.

In **1972** Stein am Rhein became the first place ever to receive the **Wakker Prize**. This prize is awarded by the **Swiss Heritage Society** to municipalities that take particularly good care of their townscape. The residents make sure that the old houses are preserved. That is why Stein am Rhein is regarded as one of the most beautiful little towns in Switzerland.

gewusst: Part of Stein am Rhein lies on the other side of the Rhine; a bridge links the two banks.
The Wakker Prize has been awarded every year to a Swiss municipality since 1972.

teile.einleitung: Valère is a fortified church on a hill above Sion, the capital of the Valais. Together with the castle ruin of Tourbillon on the neighbouring hill, it is the landmark of the town.
wichtigste: Valère stands on a hill above Sion in the canton of the Valais.
The fortified church was built in the Middle Ages.
On the neighbouring hill stands the castle ruin of Tourbillon.
Valère and Tourbillon are the landmark of Sion.
In Valère stands one of the oldest playable organs in the world.
Today part of the Valais History Museum is housed in Valère.

abschnitte.text: Two rocky hills rise above the old town of **Sion**. On one stands the fortified church of **Valère**, on the other the castle ruin of **Tourbillon**. You can see them from far away in the **Rhône valley**. That is why they are the landmark of the capital of the Valais. A footpath leads up from the old town.

Valère is a **fortified church**: a church protected by walls like a castle. It was built in the 12th and 13th centuries. In the past, canons lived here, that is, clergy of the church of Sion. Inside there are old wall paintings and wood carvings. Especially well known is the **organ**, which was built in the 15th century and is still played today.

On the higher hill stands **Tourbillon**. The castle was built around 1300 for the Bishop of Sion. In 1788 it was gutted by fire in a great fire in the town. Since then it has been a **ruin**. From the top there is a wide view over the Valais.

Part of the **Valais History Museum** is now housed in Valère. There you can see objects from the history of the canton. In summer, organ concerts take place in the church. Many school classes and tourists visit the two hills.

gewusst: The organ of Valère is regarded as one of the oldest organs in the world that can still be played.
Between the two hills lies a small saddle, over which you can walk from Valère to Tourbillon.

teile.einleitung: Swissminiatur is an open-air park in Melide in the canton of Ticino. There you can see Switzerland in miniature: famous buildings, railways and landscapes as models.
wichtigste: Swissminiatur lies in Melide on Lake Lugano.
It opened in 1959.
The park shows over a hundred models from all over Switzerland.
The models are built at a scale of 1 to 25.
Small trains and boats run through the park.

abschnitte.text: In Swissminiatur stand models of well-known buildings from all parts of the country. They include castles, churches, bridges and railway stations. A **scale of 1 to 25** means that one metre on the real building is four centimetres in the model. So in one afternoon you can walk through the whole of Switzerland.

Many small **model trains** run through the park on long tracks. They show how important the **railway** is for Switzerland. There are also cable cars and boats in miniature. Between the models, flowers and small trees grow so that everything looks like a real landscape.

**Melide** lies on the shore of **Lake Lugano**, not far from Lugano. Here the causeway runs from Melide to Bissone across the lake, carrying a road and a railway line. Swissminiatur is usually open from spring to autumn. It is one of the well-known destinations for outings in Ticino.

gewusst: Swissminiatur has existed for over 60 years.
Because the models stand outside all year round, they have to be looked after and repaired regularly.

teile.einleitung: The Toggenburg is a valley region in the canton of St Gallen. The Thur flows through the valley. The area is known for its mountains, its folk music and hiking.
wichtigste: The Toggenburg is in the canton of St Gallen.
The Thur rises in the uppermost Toggenburg and flows through the whole valley.
Above the valley stand the Churfirsten and the Säntis.
Wildhaus is the birthplace of the reformer Huldrych Zwingli.
The Toggenburg is known for natural yodelling and folk music.

abschnitte.text: The Toggenburg stretches from the area around **Wildhaus** in the south to near **Wil** in the north. The **Thur** flows through the valley. Important places are **Wattwil**, **Lichtensteig** and **Ebnat-Kappel**. The little town of Lichtensteig has a well-preserved old town. In the upper part lie villages such as Unterwasser and Alt St Johann.

In the south of the valley stand the **Churfirsten**, a row of seven peaks. On the other side they fall steeply to **Lake Walen**. In the north the **Säntis** rises in the Alpstein. In winter you can go **skiing** in the Toggenburg, in summer walking. Cable cars take you, for example, up the Chäserrugg.

The Toggenburg is known for **natural yodelling**, singing without words. Instruments such as the **Halszither** (a kind of zither) are also part of the tradition. Near Alt St Johann and Wildhaus there is the **Klangwelt Toggenburg** (Toggenburg Sound World) with sound trails to try out. In summer the farmers solemnly drive their cattle up to the alp.

In **Wildhaus** the reformer **Huldrych Zwingli** was born in **1484**. You can still visit his birthplace today. For a long time the Toggenburg belonged to the abbey of St Gallen. Since 1803 it has been part of the canton of St Gallen. In the past the valley was also known for **textile production**.

gewusst: The Toggenburg goat is a breed of goat named after the valley.
The Churfirsten look gentle from the north but like a steep wall from the south.

teile.einleitung: Lake Sihl lies near Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz. It is the largest reservoir in Switzerland by area and supplies water for generating electricity.
wichtigste: Lake Sihl lies near Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz.
It is the largest reservoir in Switzerland by area.
The River Sihl was dammed in the 1930s.
With the water, the Etzel power station generates electricity, mainly for the railways.
In summer you can swim in Lake Sihl; in winter it often freezes over.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Sihl** is not a natural lake but a **reservoir**. It was created when the **River Sihl** was held back by a dam. The lake was fully filled in **1937**, so around 90 years ago. It is the **largest reservoir by area** in Switzerland. Because it lies on a high plateau, it is not very deep.

The water of Lake Sihl is used for the **Etzel power station**. Through a tunnel and pipes it flows down to **Altendorf** on Lake Zurich. On the way it drops a great height and drives **turbines**. This produces **electricity**, which is used above all for **SBB** trains. Hydropower is an important source of electricity in Switzerland.

Many families had to leave their homes for the reservoir. Farms, houses and parts of villages disappeared under the water. The people were resettled, which was hard for many of them. So that you can cross the lake, bridges were built, for example at **Willerzell**. Not far away lies the famous **Einsiedeln Abbey**.

Today Lake Sihl is a popular place for outings. In summer you can **swim**, sail, windsurf and barbecue on the shore. Walking and cycling paths lead around the lake. In winter the lake freezes over in cold years. Then you can sometimes go **ice skating** on it, but only if the authorities have declared the ice safe.

gewusst: Lake Sihl lies at almost 900 metres above sea level, higher than Lake Zurich.
When a lot of water is needed for electricity in winter, the water level of the lake drops noticeably.

teile.einleitung: UEFA is the football association of Europe. It organises major tournaments such as the Champions League and the European Championship. Its headquarters are in Nyon on Lake Geneva in the canton of Vaud.
wichtigste: UEFA is short for “Union des Associations Européennes de Football”.
UEFA was founded in Basel in 1954.
Its headquarters are in Nyon in the canton of Vaud.
Its members are the national football associations of Europe.
It organises the Champions League and the European Championship.
Tournaments for women and juniors are also part of it.

abschnitte.text: **UEFA** is an **umbrella organisation**. Its members are not clubs but the national **football associations** of the European countries. The **Swiss Football Association** belongs to it too. UEFA is one of six continental confederations. It belongs to the world football body **FIFA**, which has its headquarters in Zurich.

The best-known club competition is the **UEFA Champions League**. There the best clubs in Europe play against each other. Besides it there is the **Europa League** and other competitions. For national teams UEFA organises the **European Championship**. The women's European Championship and tournaments for juniors are also part of it.

UEFA was founded in **Basel** in **1954**. At first it had its seat in Paris, later in Bern. Since the 1990s it has been in **Nyon** in the canton of Vaud. Its headquarters stand there right on **Lake Geneva**. The draws for many tournaments also take place here.

UEFA sets out how its competitions are run. It trains referees and supports the development of young players. It distributes money from the tournaments to its member associations. It also campaigns against racism and violence in stadiums.

gewusst: Several large sports federations have their seat in Switzerland, for example the International Olympic Committee in Lausanne.
In 2008 Switzerland, together with Austria, hosted the men's European Football Championship.

teile.einleitung: The Vallée de Joux is a high valley in the Vaud Jura, near the border with France. It is world-famous for its watchmaking workshops, where fine and complicated watches have been made for centuries.
wichtigste: The Vallée de Joux lies in the Jura in the canton of Vaud.
The valley lies at about 1,000 metres above sea level.
In the valley lies the Lac de Joux, the largest lake in the Jura.
Important places are Le Sentier and Le Brassus.
Famous watch companies have their headquarters here.
The winters are long and cold.

abschnitte.titel: A high valley in the Jura
abschnitte.text: The Vallée de Joux lies in the **Jura** in the west of the canton of Vaud, at about 1,000 metres above sea level. In the valley lies the **Lac de Joux**, the largest lake of the Jura mountains. Beside it is the small Lac Brenet. The valley belongs to three municipalities: Le Chenit, L'Abbaye and Le Lieu. The best-known villages are **Le Sentier** and **Le Brassus**.

In the past the people of the valley lived from farming. In the long winter there was little to do. So many families began to make **watch parts** at home. In time a great craft grew up. Today well-known **watchmaking manufactures** have their headquarters in the valley. There especially fine watches with complicated movements are built.

A **manufacture** is a workshop in which much is done by hand. The watchmakers assemble tiny gear wheels, springs and screws. Some watches have **complications**, for example a moon phase or a calendar. Such a watch takes a great deal of patience and experience. The watchmaking craft of Switzerland and France is part of UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage.

In winter it is often very cold in the Vallée de Joux. When the **Lac de Joux** freezes, you can skate on it. The valley is also popular with cross-country skiers. In summer many people walk and swim at the lake. Forests and pastures shape the quiet landscape.

gewusst: In winter the Lac de Joux can freeze so thickly that you can skate on it over long distances.
The watchmaking craft of Switzerland and France was added to UNESCO's intangible cultural heritage in 2020.

t1we3l07.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Aargau

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Aargau is divided into two halves. On the left a white river flows over a black ground, on the right three white stars stand on a blue ground.
wichtigste: The Aargau coat of arms is divided vertically into two halves.
On the left is a white, wavy river on black.
On the right are three white stars on blue.
The river stands for the Aare.
The coat of arms came about in 1803, when the canton was founded.

abschnitte.titel: What the coat of arms looks like
abschnitte.text: The **coat of arms of the canton of Aargau** is divided vertically into two halves. On the left side a **white, wavy river** flows over a **black** ground. On the right side stand **three white stars** on a **blue** ground. The canton's flag looks exactly the same.

The river stands for the **Aare**, which also gave the canton its name. The three stars are often interpreted as the areas from which the canton was put together. But there are different opinions about the exact meaning. What is clear: the coat of arms was meant to show something new and not to recall old rulers.

The canton of Aargau was founded in **1803**. At that time Napoleon reorganised Switzerland with the Act of Mediation. Areas that had previously belonged to others became a canton of their own. At the same time Aargau received its new coat of arms. The main town is **Aarau**.

gewusst: Together with St Gallen, Graubünden, Thurgau, Ticino and Vaud, Aargau is one of the cantons that were newly created in 1803.

teile.einleitung: The Tödi is the highest mountain in the canton of Glarus. It is around 3,600 metres high and stands on the border with the canton of Graubünden. Because of its size it is often called the “king of the Glarus Alps”.
wichtigste: The Tödi is around 3,600 metres high.
It is the highest mountain in the canton of Glarus.
It lies on the border between Glarus and Graubünden.
There are large glaciers on the Tödi.
The Linth rises near it.

abschnitte.text: The Tödi has several peaks. The highest is called **Piz Russein** and is **3,614 metres** high. The mountain is so broad and massive that you can recognise it from many directions. It belongs to the **Glarus Alps**. Its flanks are covered with **glaciers**, which are getting smaller, as everywhere in the Alps.

The border between the **canton of Glarus** and the **canton of Graubünden** runs over the Tödi. On the Glarus side lies the valley of **Linthal**. On the Graubünden side lies the Surselva with the village of **Disentis**. Very close to the mountain rises the **Linth**, the most important river in the canton of Glarus.

The Tödi was first climbed in **1824**. Even today the ascent is demanding. You have to cross glaciers and need good **mountaineering equipment**. Along the route there are **mountain huts** of the Swiss Alpine Club, where climbers spend the night. Without experience or a mountain guide you should not climb up there.

The meltwater from the glaciers flows down into the valley. In the area around the Tödi, water is also used to generate **electricity**. There are reservoirs and power stations for this. A well-known example is the **Linth-Limmern power station** in the canton of Glarus.

gewusst: For the people of Glarus the Tödi is a landmark of their canton.
The name Tödi is very old, and its origin is not known for certain.

t1wibla4.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Landschaft

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Landschaft shows a red Basel crozier with small projections on a white ground. This clearly distinguishes it from the black Basel crozier of Basel-Stadt.
wichtigste: In the coat of arms of Basel-Landschaft is a red Basel crozier.
The ground is white.
On the staff are small projections, called crockets.
The Basel crozier of Basel-Stadt, by contrast, is black.
The canton of Basel-Landschaft was created in 1833.

abschnitte.text: In the coat of arms of **Basel-Landschaft** you can see a **red Basel crozier** on a **white** ground. On the curved part of the staff sit small projections. They are called **crockets**. The staff is turned the other way from the one in the coat of arms of Basel-Stadt. This way you can tell at a glance which canton is meant.

In the past the town and the countryside belonged together in the canton of Basel. But the people in the countryside felt disadvantaged because the town had more say. After disputes and fighting, the two separated in **1833**. This is how the half-cantons of **Basel-Stadt** and **Basel-Landschaft** came about. The main town of Basel-Landschaft is **Liestal**.

The **Basel crozier** recalls the staff of the former Bishop of Basel. Basel-Stadt kept the **black** staff. Basel-Landschaft chose a **red** staff with crockets. The coat of arms of the town of Liestal is also red and white. So the coat of arms shows the link with the city of Basel and yet its independence.

gewusst: The crozier in the Basel-Landschaft coat of arms faces the other way from the one of Basel-Stadt, so the two seem to be turning their backs on each other.

teile.einleitung: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are called the Original Cantons. According to tradition, they were the first to join together in 1291. In time this alliance grew into the Confederation and later into present-day Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Original Cantons are Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden.
Today Unterwalden consists of Obwalden and Nidwalden.
The Federal Charter of 1291 is regarded as an important early alliance.
According to legend, their representatives swore an oath on the Rütli.
The name “Switzerland” comes from the canton of Schwyz.
The Original Cantons are also called the Forest Cantons (Waldstätte).

abschnitte.text: In the **Federal Charter** of **1291** the valley communities of **Uri**, **Schwyz** and **Unterwalden** promised to help one another. They wanted to defend themselves together against foreign rulers and against strife. The Federal Charter is written in **Latin**. Today it is kept in the **Federal Charters Museum** in Schwyz. The 1st of August, the **national holiday**, recalls this alliance.

According to **legend**, representatives of the three valley communities met on the **Rütli meadow** on Lake Uri. There they are said to have sworn an **oath** to stand by one another. This story is called the **Rütli Oath**. Whether it happened exactly like this is not proved. Even so, the Rütli meadow is an important place of remembrance in Switzerland.

The Original Cantons are also called the **Waldstätte** (Forest Cantons). They lie around the lake, which is therefore called **Lake Lucerne** (in German: Vierwaldstättersee, “Lake of the Four Forest Cantons”). Later Lucerne was added as the fourth place. **Unterwalden** was divided into two parts early on: **Obwalden** and **Nidwalden**. Today they are two separate cantons with one seat each in the Council of States.

In time further places joined the alliance, for example **Lucerne**, **Zurich** and **Bern**. This is how the **Old Swiss Confederacy** came about. Other peoples soon called all the Confederates after the canton of **Schwyz**. From this came the name **Switzerland**. The Swiss flag also recalls the red banner of Schwyz.

gewusst: The Federal Charter of 1291 is not the only early alliance, but in the 19th century it was declared the most important founding document.
The coat of arms of Schwyz is red with a small white cross.

teile.einleitung: The Uetliberg is the local mountain of the city of Zurich. It lies on the western edge of the city and is just under 870 metres high. From the top there is a wide view over the city, Lake Zurich and the Alps.
wichtigste: The Uetliberg is Zurich's local mountain.
It is just under 870 metres high.
It belongs to the Albis chain.
A railway runs from Zurich main station almost to the summit.
On the summit stands a lookout tower.
A planet trail leads from the Uetliberg to the Felsenegg.

abschnitte.text: A **Hausberg** (“local mountain”) is a mountain so close to a city that many people can visit it quickly. For Zurich that is the **Uetliberg**. It belongs to the **Albis chain**, a chain of hills west of Lake Zurich. Its summit is called **Uto Kulm**. It is covered with forest and is a popular destination for outings.

From **Zurich main station** the **Uetliberg railway** runs in about 20 minutes to just below the summit. It is one of the steepest railways in Switzerland that runs without a rack. From the terminus you are at the top in a few minutes. But many people also walk up from the city.

On the summit stands a **lookout tower**. From there you can see the whole **city of Zurich** and **Lake Zurich**. In clear weather the view reaches far to the **Alps**. In autumn there is often **fog** over the valley while the sun shines at the top. Then it looks as if you were standing above a sea of clouds.

From the Uetliberg the **planet trail** leads along the ridge to the **Felsenegg**. Along the way stand models of the **Sun** and the planets. Their sizes and distances are scaled down accurately. So as you walk you realise how huge our solar system is. From the Felsenegg an aerial cable car runs down to Adliswil.

gewusst: In the Middle Ages there was a castle on the Uetliberg, of which only traces remain.
When there is snow, many people from Zurich go sledging on the Uetliberg.

teile.einleitung: The Seerücken is a long, wooded ridge of hills in the canton of Thurgau. It lies between the Untersee, part of Lake Constance, and the valley of the Thur.
wichtigste: The Seerücken is in the canton of Thurgau.
It stretches along the southern shore of the Untersee.
It separates the Lake Constance area from the valley of the Thur.
The ridge is covered with woods, meadows, orchards and small villages.
It was shaped by glaciers in the ice age.

abschnitte.text: The **Seerücken** is a long ridge of hills in the north of the **canton of Thurgau**. On one side it slopes down to the **Untersee**, on the other to the **Thur valley**. Its shape recalls a back, which is where the name comes from (“Rücken” means back, “See” means lake). It is not very high, but you can see it from far away. From its viewpoints you can look across the lake as far as Germany.

The Seerücken was shaped by the **glaciers of the ice age**. At that time the Rhine glacier reached far into Thurgau. It pushed rubble and sand ahead of it and smoothed the landscape. When the ice melted, hills and hollows were left behind. In some hollows small lakes and bogs formed.

On the Seerücken there are many **farms**, **woods** and **orchards**. Thurgau is known for its apples and is often called “**Mostindien**” (“Cider India”). At the foot of the Seerücken, on the Untersee, lie places such as **Steckborn** and **Ermatingen**. On the slope above Mannenbach stands **Arenenberg Castle** with the Napoleon Museum.

gewusst: The Seerücken is good for walking and cycling, with views of Lake Constance.
The Untersee is the smaller, western part of Lake Constance.

teile.einleitung: The Tectonic Arena Sardona is a mountain area in the cantons of Glarus, St Gallen and Graubünden. Since 2008 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site, because you can see there especially well how mountains are formed.
wichtigste: The Tectonic Arena Sardona lies in Glarus, St Gallen and Graubünden.
It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008.
There, older layers of rock lie on top of younger ones.
This feature is called the Glarus Main Thrust.
Also well known is the Martinsloch, a hole in a rock wall.

abschnitte.text: Normally **younger layers of rock** lie on top and older ones underneath. In the Tectonic Arena Sardona it is the other way round. There, very old rock was pushed over much younger rock. This line is called the **Glarus Main Thrust**. On many mountains you can see it as a clear line in the rock face.

The Alps were formed because two great **tectonic plates** moved against each other. In the process, layers of rock were pushed together, folded and stacked on top of each other. This movement is called **tectonics**. It lasted for millions of years. In the Tectonic Arena Sardona you can see this process on the surface especially well.

As early as the 19th century, geologists studied these mountains. For a long time they argued about how old rock could end up on young rock. The explanation of the **thrust** helped to give a better understanding of how the Alps were formed. That is why the area is known worldwide for **geology**.
