In the **Tschingelhörner** above Elm in the canton of Glarus there is a large hole in the rock, the **Martinsloch**. On a few days in spring and autumn the sun shines through this hole. Its light then falls exactly on the church tower of **Elm**. Many people come to see this spectacle.

gewusst: The name Sardona comes from the Piz Sardona, a mountain in the area.
The Tectonic Arena Sardona was the first UNESCO World Heritage Site in the canton of Glarus.

teile.einleitung: Walchwil is a municipality in the canton of Zug. It lies on a sunny slope on the eastern shore of Lake Zug, at the foot of the Rossberg.
wichtigste: Walchwil is in the canton of Zug.
The municipality lies on the eastern shore of Lake Zug.
It lies at the foot of the Rossberg.
The slope is sunny and the climate mild.
The railway line from Zug to Arth-Goldau runs through Walchwil.

abschnitte.text: **Walchwil** lies on the **eastern shore of Lake Zug**, between the town of Zug and Arth. The village climbs a steep slope from the shore. Above it rise the **Zugerberg** and the **Rossberg**. From the village you can see far across the lake to the Rigi.

Because the slope faces west, the sun shines in Walchwil until the evening. The lake stores warmth and makes the climate **mild**. That is why plants that generally like it warm grow here, for example **sweet chestnuts**. Many people like living here because of the lovely view.

On the lakeshore the **railway line** from Zug to Arth-Goldau runs through Walchwil. A road also runs along the lake. So you can quickly reach Zug or central Switzerland. On the shore there are swimming spots and a small harbour.

gewusst: From Walchwil you can see across Lake Zug to the Rigi.

teile.einleitung: The Tell Plays Altdorf are a theatre in the main town of the canton of Uri. Friedrich Schiller's play “William Tell” is performed there, acted mainly by people from the region.
wichtigste: The Tell Plays take place in Altdorf in the canton of Uri.
The play performed is Schiller's “William Tell”.
The Tell Plays have existed since 1899.
They are performed in their own theatre, the Tellspielhaus.
The actors are mostly amateurs from the region.

abschnitte.text: The **Tell Plays Altdorf** were founded in **1899**. Since then Schiller's **“William Tell”** has been staged again and again in Altdorf. The performances do not take place every year but at intervals of a few years. Every new season is staged afresh, that is, newly rehearsed and designed.

For the performances Altdorf has a theatre of its own, the **Tellspielhaus**. It was built in the 1920s. The performers rehearse and play here. Many of them are **amateurs**, that is, not professional actors. They live in the canton of Uri and take part in their free time.

**Friedrich Schiller** was a famous German poet. His play “William Tell” was first performed in **1804**. It tells the legend of the shot at the apple and of the struggle of the people of central Switzerland against the bailiffs. Schiller himself was never in Switzerland. Even so, his play has shaped the image of Tell to this day.

Altdorf is closely linked to the **Tell legend**. According to tradition, the **shot at the apple** took place here. On the village square stands a large **Tell Monument** from 1895. It shows Tell with his crossbow and his son Walter.

gewusst: Schiller's “William Tell” is also performed in other places, for example in Interlaken.
A well-known line from the play is: “Through this hollow way he must come.”

teile.einleitung: The Untersee is the western part of Lake Constance. At its end the Rhine leaves the lake at Stein am Rhein. From Schaffhausen you can travel by boat up the Rhine to the Untersee.
wichtigste: Lake Constance consists of the Obersee and the Untersee.
The Untersee lies between Switzerland and Germany.
On the Swiss shore lies the canton of Thurgau.
At Stein am Rhein the Rhine flows out of the Untersee.
In the Untersee lies the island of Reichenau, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Boats run between Schaffhausen, Stein am Rhein and the Untersee.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Constance** consists of two large parts: the **Obersee** (Upper Lake) and the **Untersee** (Lower Lake). At **Konstanz** they are linked by a short stretch of the Rhine, the **Seerhein**. The Untersee is smaller and less deep than the Obersee. It has many bays and peninsulas. The southern shore belongs to the **canton of Thurgau**, the northern shore to Germany.

From **Schaffhausen** passenger boats travel up the **Rhine**. On the way they pass Diessenhofen and **Stein am Rhein**. Then they reach the **Untersee** and continue as far as **Kreuzlingen** and Konstanz. The journey passes woods, castles and old little towns. It is regarded as one of the most beautiful **river trips** in Europe.

In the Untersee lies the island of **Reichenau**. It belongs to Germany. In the Middle Ages an important **monastery** stood there. Some old churches from that time have survived to this day. That is why the island is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. Today a lot of **vegetables** are grown on the Reichenau.

On the Swiss shore lie places such as **Steckborn**, **Ermatingen** and **Berlingen**. They have old houses and small harbours. **Stein am Rhein** is famous for its painted houses in the old town. Above the Untersee, on the Seerücken, stands the **Napoleon Museum at Arenenberg**.

gewusst: Many water birds rest on the Untersee in winter.
The Rhine first flows into Lake Constance and comes out again at the Untersee.

teile.einleitung: The Spreuer Bridge is an old covered wooden bridge over the Reuss in Lucerne. It is famous for its paintings of a dance of death from the 17th century.
wichtigste: The Spreuer Bridge crosses the Reuss in Lucerne.
It is a covered wooden bridge from the Middle Ages.
Besides the Chapel Bridge it is Lucerne's second old wooden bridge.
Under the roof hang paintings of a dance of death from the 17th century.
They were painted by Kaspar Meglinger with his workshop.

abschnitte.text: The **Spreuer Bridge** crosses the **Reuss** just before it leaves Lucerne. It is built of wood and has a **roof**. It was built in the early 15th century and was part of the town's fortifications. The bridge is slightly angled and runs across an old weir. In the middle stands a small **chapel**.

The name has to do with **chaff** (“Spreu”). Chaff is the husks and remains left over when grain is threshed. In the past, chaff and leaves could only be thrown into the Reuss from this bridge. In this way the water carried the waste out of the town. It was forbidden from the other bridges.

Under the roof hang triangular **wooden panels** with paintings. They were painted in the **17th century** by the painter **Kaspar Meglinger** and his workshop. The pictures show a **dance of death**. In them Death appears as a skeleton to people of all ranks: kings, farmers, merchants and children. The message is: in the face of death all people are equal.

abschnitte.titel: The sister of the Chapel Bridge
abschnitte.text: The better-known wooden bridge in Lucerne is the **Chapel Bridge** with its water tower. It largely burned down in **1993** and was rebuilt. The Spreuer Bridge, by contrast, has been preserved in its old form. Both bridges are landmarks of Lucerne and are visited by many tourists.

gewusst: Dances of death were a popular subject for pictures across Europe in the Middle Ages and the early modern period.
The Spreuer Bridge is one of the oldest surviving wooden bridges in Europe.

teile.einleitung: St Moritz is a famous holiday resort in the Upper Engadine in the canton of Graubünden. It twice hosted the Winter Olympic Games and is world-famous for winter sports.
wichtigste: St Moritz lies in the Upper Engadine in the canton of Graubünden.
The resort lies at around 1,800 metres above sea level on Lake St Moritz.
The Winter Olympic Games took place here in 1928 and 1948.
St Moritz is regarded as the birthplace of winter tourism in the Alps.
The natural-ice bobsleigh run and the horse races on the frozen lake are well known.

abschnitte.text: **St Moritz** lies in the **Upper Engadine** in the canton of **Graubünden**. The resort is at around **1,800 metres** above sea level on a lake. High mountains rise all around, and the climate is dry and sunny. In the Engadine people speak **Romansh** as well as German. In Romansh the place is called **San Murezzan**.

abschnitte.titel: The invention of the winter holiday
abschnitte.text: In the past guests only travelled to St Moritz in summer, mainly for the **mineral springs**. In **1864** the hotelier **Johannes Badrutt** invited English guests to come in winter. If they did not like it, they would not have to pay anything, or so the story goes. The guests stayed until spring. Since then St Moritz has been regarded as the **birthplace of winter tourism** in the Alps.

St Moritz hosted the **Winter Olympic Games** in **1928** and **1948**. Few places in the world have hosted the Winter Games twice. Later, **Alpine ski world championships** were also held here several times. The **bobsleigh run** from St Moritz to Celerina is rebuilt every year from **natural ice**. Also well known is the **Cresta Run**, an ice track for sledges that you ride head first.

In winter **Lake St Moritz** freezes over. Then special events take place on the ice. At the **White Turf**, horses gallop across the snow-covered lake. There are also polo matches and other events on the ice. In summer you can walk, cycle and sail on the lakes in the area.

gewusst: In St Moritz there is a leaning church tower that tilts more than some famous towers.
One of the first electric lights in Switzerland burned in St Moritz, in a hotel.

teile.einleitung: The UNESCO Entlebuch Biosphere is a region in the canton of Lucerne. It was recognised as a biosphere reserve in 2001. The aim is to protect nature while living and working well within it.
wichtigste: The Entlebuch lies in the canton of Lucerne, between Lucerne and Bern.
Since 2001 it has been a UNESCO biosphere reserve.
It was the first biosphere reserve in Switzerland under UNESCO's new rules.
Typical features are bogs, forests and mountains such as the Schrattenflue.
Farming and tourism are meant to be in harmony with nature.

abschnitte.text: A **biosphere reserve** is an area honoured by **UNESCO**. Unlike in a national park, many people live and work there. The aim is for them to use nature **sustainably**. That means: in such a way that later generations can still live from it. Some parts of the area are strictly protected.

In the Entlebuch there are especially many **bogs**. Bogs are wet areas in which **peat** forms over a long time. Rare plants grow there, and many animals find a habitat. Also well known is the **Schrattenflue**, a limestone mountain with many grooves and holes in the rock. Such landscapes are called **karst**.

Many people in the Entlebuch work in **farming**, in trades or in **tourism**. Farms produce cheese, meat and other foods. Products from the region are sold with a label of their own. In this way more money stays in the valley, and the routes for the goods are short.

The Entlebuch is a popular area for **hiking**, and in winter for cross-country skiing and downhill skiing. There are themed trails on which you can learn a lot about bogs and nature. Well-known places are **Sörenberg** and **Flühli**. From the top station on the Brienzer Rothorn you have a wide view.

gewusst: Those entitled to vote in the Entlebuch themselves voted on whether their region should become a biosphere reserve.
Bogs store a great deal of carbon and are therefore also important for the climate.

teile.einleitung: The Verzasca Valley is a wild mountain valley in the canton of Ticino. It is known for the crystal-clear, green water of the Verzasca and for the old stone bridge Ponte dei Salti near Lavertezzo.
wichtigste: The Verzasca Valley lies in the canton of Ticino, north of Locarno.
The River Verzasca has very clear, green water.
At Lavertezzo stands the double-arched Ponte dei Salti.
At the entrance to the valley lies the Lago di Vogorno reservoir.
Sonogno is the last village in the valley.
Typical are old stone houses, the rustici.

abschnitte.text: The **Verzasca Valley** lies in **Ticino**, north of Locarno. The **Verzasca** flows through the valley. Its water is so clear that you can see right to the bottom, and it shimmers green. The river has shaped round, smooth rocks. The valley is narrow and steep, with forests and small villages.

At **Lavertezzo** the **Ponte dei Salti** spans the river. It is an old stone bridge with **two arches**. Because it is so beautiful, it is photographed very often. In summer many day-trippers come here. But the water is very cold and can be dangerous, because it can suddenly rise.

In the valley stand many **rustici**. These are old houses of grey stone, often with roofs of stone slabs. In the past people here lived from goats, cows and small fields. Many moved away because life was hard. The last village in the valley is **Sonogno**. Today the villages of the valley together form the municipality of Verzasca.

At the entrance to the valley lies the **Lago di Vogorno** reservoir. It is held back by a high **dam** at Contra. The water is used to generate electricity. The dam is also known because you can make a bungee jump into the depths from it.

gewusst: In a James Bond film a stuntman jumped from the Verzasca dam; since then it has been world-famous.
Corippo in the Verzasca Valley was for a long time the municipality with the fewest inhabitants in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: In the city of Fribourg runs a very special funicular. Since 1899 it has been operated using waste water as a counterweight, and it is one of the last railways of this kind.
wichtigste: The funicular in Fribourg opened in 1899.
It links the lower town with the upper town.
It runs without a motor, using waste water as a counterweight.
The upper car is filled with water and pulls the lower one up.
It is one of the last railways of this kind in the world.

abschnitte.text: The city of **Fribourg** is divided into a **lower town** on the Sarine and an **upper town**. Between them lies a steep slope. Since **1899** a **funicular** has run here. It links the **Neuveville** district below with the upper town. The ride is short, but it saves a tiring walk.

The special thing is its **drive**. The railway has **no motor**. Both cars hang on the same cable. Under the car at the top there is a **tank**. This is filled with **waste water** from the town. This makes the upper car heavier, so it runs down and in doing so pulls the other car up. At the bottom the water is let out again.

In the past there were many railways that worked with water as a **counterweight**. Almost all of them were later converted or shut down. The funicular in Fribourg is one of the **last of its kind** in the world. It is a **protected monument** and is run by the Fribourg transport company. It is popular with locals and visitors alike.

gewusst: You cannot smell the waste water in the railway, because it is in closed tanks.
The railway shows how energy was saved with simple physics more than 100 years ago.

teile.einleitung: Victorinox is a company from Ibach in the canton of Schwyz. It makes the world-famous red Swiss Army Knife, which in Switzerland is also called a “Sackmesser” (pocket knife).
wichtigste: Victorinox has its headquarters in Ibach near Schwyz.
The company was founded in 1884 by Karl Elsener.
It makes the red Swiss Army Knife.
The knife was originally built for the Swiss Army.
The name combines “Victoria” and “inox”.
The knives are sold all over the world.

abschnitte.text: In **1884** **Karl Elsener** founded a knife workshop in **Ibach** near Schwyz. At that time the Swiss Army still bought its soldiers' knives abroad. Elsener wanted them to be made in Switzerland. From 1891 he supplied knives to the **army**. This is how the well-known **soldier's knife** came about.

After the death of his mother Victoria, Karl Elsener named his company after her. Later the word **“inox”** was added. It stands for stainless steel, in French “inoxydable”. This is how the name **Victorinox** came about. The company emblem is a cross in a shield.

The Swiss Army Knife does not have just one blade. Depending on the model it also has a **screwdriver**, tin opener, scissors, saw or corkscrew. Everything folds away. That is why the knife fits into any trouser pocket. Best known is the red **officer's knife**.

Today Victorinox sells its knives in a great many countries. Besides pocket knives, the company also makes kitchen knives, watches and travel luggage. In 2005 Victorinox took over the company **Wenger** from Delémont, which also made pocket knives. The red Swiss Army Knife has become a symbol of Switzerland.

gewusst: Swiss Army Knives have even flown into space with astronauts.
In German the knife is called “Sackmesser”; in English it is the “Swiss Army Knife”.

teile.einleitung: St Peter is a church in the old town of Zurich. Its tower carries the largest church clock face in Europe and can be recognised from far away.
wichtigste: St Peter stands in the old town of Zurich, on the left bank of the Limmat.
It is regarded as the oldest parish church in the city.
The faces of the tower clock have a diameter of around 8.7 metres.
This is the largest church clock face in Europe.
Today St Peter is a Reformed church.

abschnitte.text: The church of **St Peter** stands on a small hill in the **old town of Zurich**, on the left bank of the **Limmat**. There was already a church at this spot in the early Middle Ages. For this reason St Peter is regarded as the **oldest parish church** in Zurich. The present nave was rebuilt in the Baroque style in the 18th century. Since the **Reformation** St Peter has been a Reformed church.

St Peter is famous for its **tower clock**. Its **faces** have a diameter of around **8.7 metres**. This is the **largest church clock face in Europe**. The minute hand alone is several metres long. In this way people all over the city could read the time in the past, including the boatmen on the Limmat.

The tower of St Peter does not belong to the church congregation but to the **city of Zurich**. In the past a **fire watchman** lived at the top of the tower. He kept a lookout for fires day and night. If he saw smoke or flames, he raised the alarm. This was important because many houses were built of wood at that time.

Some well-known pastors worked at St Peter. One of them was **Johann Caspar Lavater** in the 18th century. He was a well-known writer and thinker of his time. Today services, concerts and guided tours take place in the church. Together with the Grossmünster and the Fraumünster, St Peter is one of the well-known churches of Zurich's old town.

gewusst: The clock face of St Peter is larger than the faces of Big Ben in London.
From the Lindenhof, very close by, you have a lovely view of the old town.

teile.einleitung: Silvesterchlausen is an old custom in Appenzell Ausserrhoden. Costumed Chläuse walk from farm to farm with big bells, sing and wish everyone a happy new year.
wichtigste: Silvesterchlausen takes place in Appenzell Ausserrhoden, for example in Urnäsch.
The Chläuse go from house to house in groups called Schuppel.
They wear big bells and cowbells that can be heard from far away.
There are three kinds: the Schöne, the Schö-Wüeschte and the Wüeschte.
The Chläuse sing a Zäuerli, a natural yodel without words.
The Chläusen takes place on 31 December and on 13 January, the “old New Year's Eve”.

abschnitte.text: At **Silvesterchlausen**, groups of costumed men walk through the villages. Such a group is called a **Schuppel**. The Chläuse wear heavy **bells** and **cowbells** on their bodies. When they move in time, the bells ring loudly. The custom is best known in **Urnäsch**, but also in other municipalities in **Appenzell Ausserrhoden**.

There are **three kinds** of Chläuse. The **Schöne** (“beautiful ones”) wear splendid headdresses with little figures and scenes from life in the Appenzell region. The **Wüeschte** (“wild ones”) are dressed in **fir branches**, moss, leaves and other natural materials and wear wild masks. The **Schö-Wüeschte** are a mixture of the two: they are made of natural materials but finely and skilfully designed. The costumes are often made by hand over months.

In front of every house the Schuppel stops and forms a circle. Then the Chläuse sing a **Zäuerli**. This is a **natural yodel without words**, slow and solemn. Afterwards they ring their bells again and wish the residents a **happy new year**. The residents often thank them with a drink or a small gift of money.

The Chläusen takes place on **31 December**. In some places, such as Urnäsch, people set out again on **13 January**. This day is called “**old New Year's Eve**”. It comes from the earlier **Julian calendar**, which ran a few days behind the present calendar. Some municipalities stayed with the old date and still celebrate that way today.

gewusst: A Schuppel is often out and about early in the morning, long before sunrise.
Silvesterchlausen is one of the living traditions of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss Museum of Transport in Lucerne is a large museum about transport and mobility. It shows locomotives, ships, aeroplanes, cars and space travel and is one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Swiss Museum of Transport stands in Lucerne on Lake Lucerne.
It opened in 1959.
It shows transport by rail, road, water and air.
Space travel also has an area of its own.
The museum includes a planetarium and a large cinema.
It is one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Museum of Transport** stands in **Lucerne**, close to the shore of Lake Lucerne. It opened in **1959**. Since then it has grown a great deal and today has several large halls. Every year a great many visitors come. This makes it one of the most visited museums in Switzerland.

In the hall for **rail transport** stand real locomotives and carriages, from old steam locomotives to modern trains. You find out how the railway changed Switzerland, for example through the building of the Gotthard tunnel. In the **road transport** area you can see cars, bicycles and PostBuses. You can try out a lot of things yourself.

The **shipping** area is about steamships and ports. In **aviation** there are real aeroplanes and helicopters. A separate part shows **space travel** and how people journey into space. Cable cars and mountain railways also have their place, because they are especially important in Switzerland.

The museum includes a **planetarium**. There you can see the starry sky on a round dome. In the large **cinema**, films are shown on a huge screen. There is also an exhibition about chocolate and a museum with works by the artist **Hans Erni**.

gewusst: In the museum there is a huge walk-on aerial photograph of Switzerland, on which you can walk from canton to canton.
In the museum you can look at real locomotives and aeroplanes close up.

teile.einleitung: The Sonderbund War was a short civil war in Switzerland in November 1847. It was followed in 1848 by the creation of the modern federal state with a common constitution.
wichtigste: The Sonderbund was an alliance of Catholic-conservative cantons, led by Lucerne.
It included Lucerne, Uri, Schwyz, Obwalden, Nidwalden, Zug, Fribourg and the Valais.
In November 1847 war broke out with the other, liberal cantons.
The war lasted only a few weeks, and the Sonderbund was defeated.
General Guillaume Henri Dufour led the troops of the Federal Diet.
In 1848 Switzerland received a new federal constitution and became a federal state.

abschnitte.text: In the first half of the 19th century Switzerland was a loose **confederation of states**. The cantons argued about what the country should look like. The **liberals** wanted a stronger common state. The **Catholic conservatives** wanted to keep the power of the cantons and the Church. Religious questions also played a big part, such as the closing of monasteries in Aargau and the calling of **Jesuits** to Lucerne.

In **1845** seven Catholic cantons joined together in a defensive alliance. They were **Lucerne**, **Uri**, **Schwyz**, **Obwalden** and **Nidwalden**, **Zug**, **Fribourg** and the **Valais**. This alliance was called the **Sonderbund** (“separate alliance”). **Lucerne** was the leading place and the seat of the war council. The majority of cantons in the **Federal Diet** regarded the Sonderbund as illegal and demanded that it be dissolved.

In **November 1847** war broke out. The troops of the Federal Diet were led by General **Guillaume Henri Dufour** from Geneva. First **Fribourg** surrendered, then the troops marched against **Lucerne**. After a battle at **Gisikon**, Lucerne fell too. The war lasted less than a month. Dufour ordered his soldiers to treat prisoners and the wounded well, so there were comparatively few deaths.

abschnitte.titel: The road to the federal state
abschnitte.text: After the war the Sonderbund was dissolved. As early as **1848** Switzerland gave itself a new **federal constitution**. The confederation of states became a **federal state** with a parliament, a **Federal Council** and a common currency. **Bern** became the seat of the federal authorities. The cantons kept many tasks of their own, as is still the case today.

gewusst: The Sonderbund War was the last war fought on Swiss territory.
General Dufour was also a cartographer: he directed the making of the first accurate national map of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Seealpsee is a mountain lake in the Alpstein in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden. It lies below the Ebenalp and is a popular hiking destination with a wonderful view of the rock walls.
wichtigste: The Seealpsee lies in the Alpstein in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden.
It is below the Ebenalp at over 1,100 metres above sea level.
You reach it on foot, usually from Wasserauen.
Hiking trails lead around the lake, and there are mountain inns.
The lake is one of the best-known photo subjects in eastern Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The **Seealpsee** lies in the **Alpstein**, the mountain range around the Säntis. Steep limestone cliffs surround the lake on several sides. Above it lies the **Ebenalp**, a popular viewpoint mountain. The water is often green or blue and reflects the mountains. A stream flows out of the lake down into the valley.

There is **no public road** for cars to the Seealpsee. Most hikers start in **Wasserauen**, where the Appenzell railway ends. From there it is about an hour's walk uphill. You can also take the cable car up to the Ebenalp and walk down to the lake. On the way you pass the **Wildkirchli** and the **Aescher** mountain inn.

On the shore of the lake there are **mountain inns** where you can eat and stay overnight. In summer cows graze on the alpine meadows around the lake. The name **Seealp** simply means “alp by the lake”. Many families stop here, have picnics and enjoy the peace.

gewusst: The Seealpsee is a popular destination for photographers, especially at sunrise.
In winter the lake often freezes over and lies still in the snow.

teile.einleitung: The Stockalper Palace in Brig is a large palace with three towers. It was built in the 17th century by the wealthy Valais merchant Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper.
wichtigste: The Stockalper Palace stands in Brig in the canton of the Valais.
It was built in the 17th century by Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper.
Stockalper became very rich through trade over the Simplon Pass.
The palace has three tall towers with onion domes.
It is the landmark of Brig.

abschnitte.text: The **Stockalper Palace** is the **landmark of Brig**. It was built in the 17th century and was at that time one of the largest private buildings in Switzerland. Especially striking are the **three tall towers** with their onion domes. They bear the names of the Three Wise Men: **Kaspar**, **Melchior** and **Balthasar**. Inside lies a large **arcaded courtyard** with arched galleries on several floors.

The builder was **Kaspar Jodok von Stockalper**. He lived in the 17th century and was a very skilful **merchant**. He controlled the trade over the **Simplon Pass** between the Valais and Italy. Especially important was **salt**, which was needed in those days to preserve food. This made Stockalper one of the richest men of his time. He was also called the “**King of the Simplon**”.

So that goods could cross the mountains safely, Stockalper had the mule track over the Simplon improved. Goods were carried back and forth by mules. On the way he had houses built for overnight stays and storage. Today you can walk the **Stockalper Way** in the footsteps of these muleteers.

Stockalper had great influence and held many offices in the Valais. In time he became too powerful for some people. He was removed from office and had to flee for some years to **Domodossola** in Italy. Later he returned to Brig, where he died. His palace now belongs to the municipality of Brig and can be visited.

gewusst: The three towers of the Stockalper Palace are named after the Three Wise Men.
Concerts and festivals are held in the arcaded courtyard of the palace today.

teile.einleitung: Tête de Moine is a Swiss semi-hard cheese from the Jura Arc. It is not cut into slices but scraped with a crank into fine rosettes.
wichtigste: Tête de Moine means “monk's head” in English.
It originally comes from Bellelay Abbey in the Bernese Jura.
It is made in the Jura Arc, including the Franches-Montagnes in the canton of Jura.
It is scraped into rosettes with a device called a Girolle.
It carries the protected designation of origin AOP.

abschnitte.text: Tête de Moine goes back to the monks of **Bellelay Abbey** in the Bernese Jura. They were making this cheese centuries ago. The name means **“monk's head”**. How exactly it got this name is told in different ways. Today Bellelay is no longer a monastery, but the cheese has remained.

Tête de Moine is not cut. You put the round cheese on a spindle and turn a blade over it with a **crank**. This device is called a **Girolle** and was invented in 1982. This produces thin, frilly **rosettes** that look like little flowers. Scraping exposes the cheese to a lot of air, and it tastes especially spicy.

Tête de Moine is made in the **Jura Arc**. This includes parts of the **Bernese Jura** and of the **canton of Jura**, such as the **Franches-Montagnes**. **Raw milk** from cows of the region is used. The wheels mature for several months on wooden boards. Since 2001 the name has been protected as **AOP**, which means that only cheese from this area may be called by this name.

The rosettes are often eaten as an **apéritif snack** with bread. On a cheese platter they look especially beautiful. You can also use them to decorate salads. Today Tête de Moine is sold in many countries.

gewusst: Before the Girolle, the cheese used to be scraped thin with a knife.
The rosettes taste different from a thick slice of the same cheese.

teile.einleitung: Lake Lucerne lies in central Switzerland and is one of the largest lakes lying entirely within Switzerland. It has many arms and borders the cantons of Lucerne, Schwyz, Uri, Nidwalden and Obwalden.
wichtigste: The city of Lucerne lies on Lake Lucerne.
The lake covers about 114 square kilometres.
It borders Lucerne, Schwyz, Uri, Nidwalden and Obwalden.
The name comes from the four Forest Cantons.
The Reuss flows through the lake.
Passenger boats and old paddle steamers sail on the lake.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Lucerne** lies in the middle of central Switzerland. It covers about **114 square kilometres** and is over 200 metres deep at its deepest point. The lake has an unusual shape with many **arms** and bays. One of them is Lake Uri in the south. The **Reuss** flows in at Flüelen and out again at Lucerne.

The name comes from the **four Forest Cantons**. This is what the places Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Lucerne used to be called. Today five cantons border the lake: **Lucerne**, **Schwyz**, **Uri**, **Nidwalden** and **Obwalden**. On the southern shore lie places in Nidwalden such as **Hergiswil**, **Buochs** and **Beckenried**.

At the north-western end of the lake lies the city of **Lucerne**. From there boats sail to many places on the lake. Around the lake stand well-known mountains such as the **Rigi**, **Pilatus** and the Stanserhorn. On the western shore of Lake Uri lies the **Rütli meadow**, an important place in Swiss history.

On Lake Lucerne there is a large fleet of **passenger boats**. Especially popular are the old **paddle steamers**. They are driven by steam and have large paddle wheels at the sides. Many people use the boats for outings, and some also for getting to work.

gewusst: Five historic paddle steamers still sail on Lake Lucerne, which is one of the largest steamer fleets on a Swiss lake.
With the boat and the rack railway you can travel from Lucerne right up to the Rigi.

teile.einleitung: The University of Fribourg is a university in the city of Fribourg in the canton of Fribourg. It is bilingual: you can study in German, in French or in both languages.
wichtigste: The University of Fribourg was founded in 1889.
It is the only bilingual full university in Switzerland.
You can study in German, French or both languages.
Fribourg lies on the language border between German and French.
There are several faculties, for example law, theology and natural sciences.

abschnitte.text: The city of **Fribourg** lies exactly on the **language border**. Part of the population speaks French, another part German. The university too is **bilingual**. Students can attend their courses in **German**, in **French** or in both languages. Anyone who studies in both languages can receive a bilingual degree.

The university was founded in **1889**. It has a long **Catholic** tradition and is still known today for its faculty of **theology**. In time many other subjects were added. Today it is a university for people of all religions and backgrounds.

The university has several **faculties**. These are large departments for different fields of knowledge. They include **law**, **theology**, the humanities, economics and **natural sciences** with medicine. There are buildings in different parts of the city, for example **Miséricorde** and **Pérolles**.

Students come to Fribourg from **all over Switzerland** and from many other countries. The university is especially popular with young people who want to learn a second national language. So **German-speaking Switzerland** and **French-speaking Switzerland** meet here. The city of Fribourg is therefore also a lively student town.

gewusst: In French the city is called Fribourg and the university Université de Fribourg.
The old town of Fribourg lies high above the Sarine, which flows through a deep gorge.

tvwrptf.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden shows an upright black bear on a white ground. The bear is the heraldic animal of both Appenzells.
wichtigste: In the coat of arms of Appenzell Innerrhoden stands a bear.
The bear is black and stands upright.
The ground of the coat of arms is white.
Unlike in Ausserrhoden, there are no letters next to it.
The bear recalls the Abbey of St Gallen and Saint Gallus.

abschnitte.text: In the coat of arms of **Appenzell Innerrhoden** a **black bear** stands upright on its hind legs. The ground is **white**. The bear has red claws and sticks out a red tongue. In contrast to the coat of arms of Ausserrhoden, there are **no letters** next to it.

In the Middle Ages the Appenzell region belonged to the **Abbey of St Gallen**. The bear comes from the abbey's coat of arms. It recalls a legend about **Saint Gallus**. A bear is said to have helped him fetch wood for the fire. That is why the bear became the heraldic animal.

In **1597** Appenzell split into two parts for reasons of faith. **Innerrhoden** stayed Catholic, Ausserrhoden became Reformed. Both kept the bear. Innerrhoden has the main town **Appenzell** and is the canton with the fewest inhabitants in Switzerland.

gewusst: Appenzell Innerrhoden is one of the few cantons that still pass their laws at a Landsgemeinde in the open air.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland is not on the sea, but it still has ports. The Swiss Rhine Ports in Basel and in Basel-Landschaft link the country with the North Sea by way of the Rhine.
wichtigste: The Swiss Rhine Ports belong to the cantons of Basel-Stadt and Basel-Landschaft.
There are port facilities in Basel-Kleinhüningen, in Birsfelden and in the Auhafen in Muttenz.
From Basel the Rhine flows through Germany and the Netherlands to the North Sea.
Fuel, grain and containers in particular come into Switzerland through the ports.
The Basel Rhine ports are considered Switzerland's gateway to the sea.

abschnitte.titel: Ports in the middle of the country
abschnitte.text: The **Swiss Rhine Ports** are a joint institution of the cantons of **Basel-Stadt** and **Basel-Landschaft**. The largest port is in **Kleinhüningen** in the north of Basel. In the canton of Basel-Landschaft there are facilities in **Birsfelden** and in the **Auhafen** in **Muttenz**. Long Rhine ships dock there and are loaded and unloaded. Cranes, warehouses and railway tracks are part of every port.

abschnitte.titel: To the sea by the Rhine
abschnitte.text: From Basel, large ships can sail on the **Rhine** all the way to the **North Sea**. The river flows through Germany and the Netherlands. Important ports at the end of the route are **Rotterdam** and **Antwerp**. There goods are transferred to ocean-going ships. In this way Switzerland is linked by water to the whole world.

Many goods that people need in everyday life arrive through the Rhine ports. They include **heating oil**, **petrol** and **diesel**, but also **grain**, animal feed, gravel and metals. **Containers**, standardised steel boxes for all kinds of goods, are becoming more and more important. A single Rhine ship can carry as much as a great many lorries. That spares the roads.

The Rhine ports are important for Switzerland's **national supply**. If roads or railway lines are disrupted, the route along the Rhine remains. **Compulsory stockpiles**, for example of fuel, are also kept in stores at the ports. At the **Dreiländereck** (Three Countries Corner) in Kleinhüningen, Switzerland, Germany and France meet.

gewusst: The ships of the Swiss ocean-going fleet, which sail the world's seas, have Basel as their home port.
When the Rhine is low, ships can only sail with half a load.

teile.einleitung: The Stanserhorn is a viewpoint mountain directly above the village of Stans in Nidwalden. It is known for its CabriO cable car with an open upper deck and for its wide views.
wichtigste: The Stanserhorn rises directly above Stans in the canton of Nidwalden.
The mountain is 1,898 metres high.
First you go up on an old funicular.
Then you continue on the CabriO cable car, which has an open upper deck.
From the summit you can see many lakes and mountains of central Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The **Stanserhorn** rises just behind the village of **Stans**. Stans is the main town of the canton of **Nidwalden**. The mountain is **1,898 metres** high. From the summit there is a wide **view** over central Switzerland. You can see many lakes, including **Lake Lucerne**, and a long chain of Alpine peaks.

The journey up the Stanserhorn begins with a **funicular**. It was built as early as the end of the **19th century**. The wooden cars still look almost as they did in the past. The railway runs from Stans to a middle station. There you change to a modern cable car.

The **CabriO** is a special **aerial cable car** with **two storeys**. Below, passengers sit in a closed cabin. Above there is an **open upper deck** without a roof. There you ride up the Stanserhorn under the open sky. The CabriO opened in **2012** and was the first cable car of its kind in the world. Its name recalls a cabriolet, a car with an open roof.

At the summit stands a **revolving restaurant**. It turns slowly in a circle, so you can enjoy the whole panorama while you eat. A short circular path leads around the summit. **Marmots** live there and can often be watched. Many families go on an outing here.

gewusst: On the open upper deck of the CabriO you feel the wind as if you were flying.
The Stanserhorn is exactly as high as the Grosser Mythen in the canton of Schwyz.

teile.einleitung: St Gallen is the main town of the canton of the same name in eastern Switzerland. The city is famous for its abbey district with the old library, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: The main town of the canton of St Gallen is also called St Gallen.
The city goes back to the monk Gallus, who lived here around 1,400 years ago.
The abbey district with the cathedral and the Abbey Library is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
In the past St Gallen was world-famous for its embroidery.
The city has a well-known university and, every year, the OLMA trade fair.

abschnitte.text: The main town has the same name as the canton: **St Gallen**. The **cantonal government** and the **cantonal parliament** work here. They have their seat in the building of the old **Pfalz** (palace) in the abbey district. St Gallen is the largest city in eastern Switzerland. It lies in a high valley between Lake Constance and the Alpstein.

The city goes back to the Irish monk **Gallus**. He settled on the Steinach in the 7th century. A large **monastery** later grew up at this spot. The town grew around the monastery. The **abbey district** with the Baroque **cathedral** has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since **1983**.

A special treasure is the **Abbey Library**. It is one of the oldest libraries in the world. The Baroque hall is splendidly decorated with woodwork and paintings. Here lie very old **books** written by hand. Visitors have to put on felt slippers to protect the wooden floor.

In the past St Gallen was world-famous for **embroidery** and fine fabrics. Around 1900 embroidery was even one of Switzerland's most important exports. Today the city is also known for its **university**. Every autumn the **OLMA** takes place, a big trade fair for farming and food. Of course that includes the **St Gallen bratwurst**.

gewusst: In the Abbey Library lies the Plan of St Gall, a drawing of a monastery that is more than 1,000 years old.
In the city of St Gallen many houses have painted and decorated oriel windows.

teile.einleitung: The Susten Pass is an Alpine pass between the canton of Uri and the canton of Bern. The pass road runs from Wassen in the Reuss valley to Innertkirchen in the Bernese Oberland.
wichtigste: The Susten Pass links Uri with Bern.
On the Uri side lies the Meiental, on the Bern side the Gadmertal.
The top of the pass is over 2,200 metres above sea level.
The road was built between 1938 and 1946.
In winter the pass is closed.
Near the top of the pass lies the Stein Glacier.

abschnitte.text: The road begins in **Wassen** in the canton of Uri. It climbs through the **Meiental** to the top of the pass. Then it runs down through the **Gadmertal** to **Innertkirchen** in the canton of Bern. On the way there are many bends, tunnels and bridges. Together with the Grimsel Pass and the Furka Pass, the Susten forms a well-known round trip.

A mule track for people and animals had long led over the Susten. The present road was built from **1938 to 1946**. It was one of the first pass roads in Switzerland that was planned for **cars** from the start. Today it is very popular with motorcyclists and cyclists. PostBuses also run over the pass in summer.

On the Bern side, close to the road, lies the **Stein Glacier**. A small lake, the **Steinsee**, has formed in front of it. All around the pass rise high mountains of the **Uri Alps**. Like almost all glaciers in the Alps, the Stein Glacier has melted a great deal in recent decades.

At over 2,200 metres there is a great deal of **snow** in winter. That is why the Susten Pass is usually **closed** from autumn until early summer. In spring large snowblowers clear the road. Only then can you drive over it again.

gewusst: The name Susten comes from an old word for a storehouse, where goods used to be stored on their way over the mountains.
The round trip over the Susten, Grimsel and Furka is one of the best-known pass journeys in Switzerland.

tzjj5cc.t: Coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Stadt

teile.einleitung: The coat of arms of the canton of Basel-Stadt shows a black Basel crozier on a white ground. The staff looks like a bishop's crook and recalls Basel's long history as a bishop's city.
wichtigste: In the Basel coat of arms is a black Basel crozier.
The ground is white.
The staff looks like a bishop's crozier.
It recalls the bishops of Basel.
Basel-Landschaft, by contrast, has a red staff.

abschnitte.text: The coat of arms of **Basel-Stadt** is very simple. On a **white** ground stands a **black Basel crozier**. At the top the staff is curved like a hook, at the bottom it tapers to a point. You see this emblem everywhere in Basel: on flags, fountains, trams and street signs.

The staff is a simplified **bishop's crozier**. A bishop carries a curved staff of this kind, which recalls a shepherd's crook. In the Middle Ages Basel was an important **bishop's city**. That is why the city chose this emblem. The **Basel Minster** used to be the bishop's church.

Since the separation of **1833** there have been two Basel cantons. **Basel-Stadt** kept the **black** staff. **Basel-Landschaft** received a **red** staff with small projections. So both cantons have a similar emblem, but one that is easy to tell apart.

gewusst: Basel-Stadt is the smallest canton in Switzerland by area.
The Basel crozier can be found on old seals and coins from the Middle Ages.
